addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## Core Behavior

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

## omnifocus
OmniFocus is a GTD task manager. Hierarchy: Folders > Projects > Tasks > Subtasks.

TASK STATES: Available, Blocked, Deferred (future defer date), Flagged, Overdue, Completed, Dropped. Planned Date is a scheduling signal only — no availability/overdue constraints.

PROJECT TYPES: "sequential" (tasks in order; first incomplete = available, rest blocked; position = dependencies), "parallel" (all available), "single_actions" (no completion goal, cannot auto-complete). The `next` field is true for the first available action in a sequential project/action group; in parallel projects, all incomplete tasks have `next: true`.

ACTION GROUPS: Task with subtasks. Parent shows `blocked: true` while subtasks are active — this is normal, not an error. Do not try to unblock it.

INHERITED STATUS: `completed`/`dropped` reflect the task's own state, not its container's. `effectivelyCompleted`/`effectivelyDropped` reflect the container's state — if true, the task's parent project or action group was completed/dropped. Task in completed project: `completed: false`, `effectivelyCompleted: true`, `available: false`. Use `available_only=True` for actionable tasks.

EFFECTIVE DATES: Dates returned by get_tasks are always effective (inherited). A task with no direct due date WILL show its project's due date in the dueDate field — this is correct behavior, not a bug. You cannot clear an inherited date at the task level. Write operations set the task's own date.

RECURRING TASKS: `completed=True` uses `mark complete`, which creates the next occurrence. This is guaranteed. WARNING: Dropping a recurring task (status='dropped') without clearing recurrence first (recurrence='') spawns the next occurrence. To stop a series: update_tasks([{"id": "...", "recurrence": "", "status": "dropped"}]).

TAGS: Represent work contexts. Tag statuses: Active (normal), On Hold (tasks excluded from Available perspective), Dropped (tag hidden from picker; does NOT affect task availability).

DEFER vs DUE: Defer = hidden until that date. Due = deadline.

- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan or design. Use when the user wants to stress-test a plan before building, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- seo-optimizer: Optimize content for search engines with keyword analysis, readability scoring, meta descriptions, and competitor comparison. Use this when users want to improve SEO, optimize blog posts, or analyze content for search performance.
- systems-thinking: Analyze problems using a Systems Thinking approach. Use when users mention "systems thinking," "systemic," "feedback loops," "unintended consequences," "root cause," "interconnected," or request analysis of complex, multi-factor problems. Guides conversation through questions and observations rather than prescriptive solutions.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

docs/product-backlog.md:32:- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
docs/product-backlog.md:35:- **Duplicate detection: three inconsistent scopes, no way to dismiss, and it misses OCR date drift.** Three separate problems in one feature on `src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte`. **(1) No dismissal.** Duplicate is derived, never stored — `detectDuplicates()` groups on the composite key `total_amount|transaction_date` (`src/lib/utils/duplicateDetection.ts:14`). An `is_duplicate` column and a `find_duplicate_receipts()` RPC once existed and were dropped (`supabase/migrations-archive/009_remove_duplicate_detection.sql`), so there is nowhere to record "I checked; these are two genuine purchases" and a legitimate pair flags forever. Open modelling question if this is built: dismissal is **pair-scoped** (you asserted A and B are distinct, so a later third copy still flags) vs **receipt-scoped** (mutes the receipt, and so hides the real duplicate when a third copy arrives) — pair-scoped looks right. **(2) Three scopes for one concept.** The row badge and yellow highlight are computed over the date-filtered list (`:396`), while the checkbox filter (`:317`) and the count badge (`:400`) are computed over `allReceipts`. So with a date filter on and the checkbox ticked, a receipt whose only partner sits outside the window is listed with no badge and no highlight; with the checkbox off, that same cross-boundary duplicate is silently invisible. **(3) Match rule is keyed on OCR's weakest field.** Exact `transaction_date` equality, when `resolveOcrReceiptDate` (`src/lib/utils/receiptDateCorrection.ts:186`) can rewrite an implausible date within a 90-day window — two photos of the same receipt can land on different dates and never group. It also ignores `merchant_name` (so $84.32 at Costco and $84.32 at the dentist on one day flag) and ignores `currency` (USD vs CAD same-day flags). Candidate rule: amount exact + date within ±3 days + normalized merchant equal, reusing `ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` (`ExpenseService.ts:321`) and reconciliation's `maxDaysDifference: 3` / `amountTolerance` (`src/lib/models/Reconciliation.ts:29`, `ReconciliationService.ts:369`) rather than inventing thresholds. Note a date _window_ breaks transitivity — A~B and B~C no longer implies A~C — so a "duplicate group" becomes a graph of pairs, an independent argument for pair-scoped dismissal. A file content hash would catch identical re-uploads with perfect precision but does nothing for two separate photos; additive, not a substitute. Punted 2026-07-26.
docs/product-backlog.md:78:- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for the nothing-found-anywhere row, but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case. The tests assert the real `422`; the PRD table is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the table or leave the note.

1	# YFL Expense Tracker
2	
3	Family expense tracking. Family members capture what they spent — mostly by
4	uploading receipt images, sometimes by typing the details in by hand — and the
5	app derives their expenses and reconciles them against imported bank activity.
6	
7	## Language
8	
9	**Family**:
10	The data-scoping unit. All Receipts, Transactions, Categories, and vendor rules
11	belong to a Family, and every access-control policy scopes to it. Each user gets
12	one solo Family auto-created at signup (`ensure_default_family()`); their
13	`is_default` Family is the one they operate on. A `families` row (`id`, `name`).
14	_Avoid_: household, account
15	
16	**Family Member**:
17	A person who belongs to a Family — a `family_members` row (`family_id`,
18	`user_id`, `role`, `status`, `is_default`). `role ∈ {owner, member}` (the creator
19	is the `owner`; role is not yet used for authorization). `status ∈ {active,
20	invited, removed}`, but only `active` rows exist until Invitations ship. A member
21	is identified for display by their primary email (from `auth.users`), which the
22	client reads only through the `get_family_members()` `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC.
23	_Avoid_: user, member, participant
24	
25	**Receipt**:
26	A record of a single purchase (merchant, amount, date). May originate from an
27	uploaded image or be entered by hand. Each Receipt maps to exactly one Expense.
28	_Avoid_: bill, purchase
29	
30	**Manual Receipt**:
31	A Receipt a person creates by typing merchant, amount, and date rather than
32	uploading an image. It has no image and is not run through OCR; the person is
33	asserting the details — including the date — directly.
34	_Avoid_: manual entry, hand receipt
35	
36	**Expense**:
37	The categorized view of a Receipt used for reporting. Derived one-to-one from a
38	Receipt — never stored on its own. Talk about Expenses when reporting or
39	categorizing; talk about Receipts when capturing.
40	_Avoid_: cost, spend
41	
42	**Area of Importance**:
43	The top tier of the spending hierarchy — e.g. Essential, Priorities, Other. A
44	family-scoped `importance_areas` row with a `sort_order`. Attaches to the
45	**Grouping**, not to individual categories, so a Grouping has exactly one
46	Importance.
47	_Avoid_: priority band, tier
48	
49	**Grouping**:
50	The middle tier of the spending hierarchy — e.g. Everyday, Home, Transportation.
51	A family-scoped `category_groups` row that belongs to one **Area of Importance**
52	and gathers many Categories. A Category with no Grouping is _Uncategorized_.
53	_Avoid_: group, bucket, section
54	
55	**Spending Report**:
56	The categorized roll-up of a year's Expenses through Category → Grouping → Area
57	of Importance, shown as a month-by-month table (the `/spending` "Table" view) or
58	the **Spending Chart**. Replaces the family's hand-built spreadsheet pivot.
59	_Avoid_: pivot table, summary
60	
61	**Spending Chart**:
62	The charted form of the **Spending Report**: stacked bars (one per Grouping,
63	stacked by month) with drilldown to Categories — the `/spending` "Chart" view.
64	_Avoid_: graph, dashboard
65	
66	**Transaction**:
67	A line of activity imported from a bank or credit-card statement, reconciled
68	against Receipts. Distinct from a Receipt: it comes from the bank, not the user.
69	_Avoid_: charge, payment
70	
71	**Split Receipt**:
72	A partial-amount Receipt carved off another. A split is a FULL Receipt record
73	(not a line-item or child), preserving the 1:1 Receipt↔Expense invariant so no
74	query or reconciliation code needs to change. Peers share a nullable, indexed
75	`split_group_id` (UUID). Created by an atomic insert-then-update — the new split
76	is inserted first, the original reduced second; if the update fails the split is
77	deleted (best-effort rollback). Both the original's and the split's
78	`matched_transaction_id` are cleared. Each split takes an optional per-split date
79	override (deferred charges: hotel/AirBnB/installments) and recomputes
80	`suspicious_date` from its own date. Splits share the original
81	`receipt_image_path` — no file is duplicated.
82	_Avoid_: line item, child receipt
83	
84	**Source File**:
85	What a person hands the app — a camera photo, a screenshot, a HEIC picked from
86	Photos, an attachment on a forwarded email. Transient: it is never stored. Only
87	its name survives, sanitized into `original_filename`, so people recognize the
88	receipt by the name they gave it. Its size and format are the app's problem to
89	absorb, not the person's.
90	_Avoid_: upload, original, the image
91	
92	**Receipt Image**:
93	The single JPEG derived from a **Source File** and stored at
94	`receipt_image_path` — the only image artifact the app keeps for a Receipt. It
95	is always JPEG: HEIC and PNG are transcoded on the way in. A PDF receipt is
96	stored unmodified and is therefore **not** a Receipt Image, which is why it has
97	no zoom. **Split Receipt** peers share one Receipt Image.
98	_Avoid_: photo, scan, original, attachment
99	
100	**Potential Duplicate**:
101	Two or more Receipts that may record the same purchase — a suspicion raised by
102	the app, never an assertion. Always _potential_: a family can legitimately hold
103	two Receipts for the same merchant, amount and day. Duplicate-ness is a property
104	of a **pair** of Receipts, not of one Receipt, and it is derived on demand rather
105	than recorded. There is currently no way for a person to settle the suspicion.
106	_Avoid_: duplicate (unqualified), copy, repeat
107	
108	## Invariants
109	
110	**Family-scoped migration invariants**:
111	When categories and vendor rules moved from user- to family-scope, duplicates
112	were deduped keeping the FIRST-created row per key; the losing rows' receipt
113	categorizations become uncategorized via `expense_categories`
114	`ON DELETE SET NULL`. Category names are unique per family, case-insensitive
115	(`unique_category_per_family` on `(family_id, LOWER(name))`); vendor patterns are
116	unique per `(family_id, vendor_pattern)`. Every family-scoped RLS policy requires
117	`family_members.status = 'active'`. These migrations do not roll back cleanly —
118	fix forward.
119	
120	**Foreign-currency reconciliation**:
121	A Receipt's `total_amount` stays in its ORIGINAL currency; `exchange_rate_to_cad`
122	is stored on the Receipt at save time (fetched once, never during
123	reconciliation). Reconciliation matches CAD receipts within a $0.01 tolerance but
124	foreign-currency receipts within 5% — rate approximation, the ~FX fee, and
125	settlement timing all move the number. Rates come from the Bank of Canada Valet
126	API (series `FXEURCAD`, `FXUSDCAD`, `FXGBPCAD`).
127	
128	**Transaction import dedup**:
129	Count-based so legitimate in-file repeats survive: for each match key it inserts
130	`max(0, fileCount − dbCount)` rows, which makes re-import idempotent. The match
131	key is scoped per family + `credit_card_type`. Excluded rows deliberately count
132	toward the DB total, so re-importing does not resurrect them.
133	
134	**Suspicious-date authority**:
135	Only OCR/automated extraction sets `suspicious_date`. Manual create and any manual
136	date edit always CLEAR it — user intent is authoritative. Saving through the
137	receipt edit modal is the confirmation action; there is no separate "confirm
138	date".
139	
140	**Suspicious-date scope**:
141	A suspicious date is a statement that the Receipt's date is untrustworthy, so
142	that date cannot also be used to decide whether the Receipt is in scope. Counting
143	or filtering flagged Receipts by the date window would hide exactly the ones
144	whose date is wrong — they have been filed into the wrong window. The flag is
145	therefore family-global, deliberately, even while the list beneath it is
146	date-filtered. Contrast **Split Receipt** grouping, where `split_group_id` is a
147	trustworthy stored fact and can be resolved globally with no such tension.
148	
149	**Size limits govern the Receipt Image, not the Source File**:
150	The 5MB image / 10MB PDF limits state what the family agrees to _store_ — they
151	describe the **Receipt Image**. A **Source File** is bounded only by a 25MB
152	ceiling, and that ceiling exists solely to stop an enormous file from exhausting
153	memory during decode; it is not a statement about acceptable receipts. Asking a
154	person to shrink a photo the app is about to shrink anyway is asking them to do
155	the code's job. See [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md).
156	
157	**Zoom never invents pixels**:
158	In the receipt viewer 100% means fit-to-viewport, not 1:1, so the zoom ceiling is
159	a property of the individual image rather than a fixed percentage: it stops at
160	that image's own natural resolution. Two consequences are deliberate. Zoom
161	disables itself entirely for an image already at or below viewport size — if
162	there are no more real pixels there is no more zoom, and a greyed-out control
163	says so honestly. And storage holds three generations of Receipt Image
164	(full-resolution from before resizing existed, 2000px, and 2400px), each of
165	which gets a correct ceiling from its own dimensions with no migration.
166	
167	**Every uploaded image becomes JPEG**:
168	HEIC and PNG are transcoded during resize; only PDFs pass through untouched. One
169	stored format means one set of rules for OCR, display, and storage accounting.
170	Resizing happens in the browser via Canvas, so this holds only for the upload
171	path — a receipt arriving by email is stored exactly as it was sent, at whatever
172	size and format the sender's mail client produced.
173	
174	**Receipt minimum-data rule**:
175	A Receipt may be saved with empty fields, but at least ONE of merchant / amount /
176	date must be non-empty.
177	
178	**Expense categorization precedence**:
179	Manual category assignments are never overwritten by auto (vendor-rule)
180	assignments — auto-categorization only touches uncategorized expenses. New
181	families get 43 default categories.
182

app derives their expenses and reconciles them against imported bank activity.

## Language

**Family**:
The data-scoping unit. All Receipts, Transactions, Categories, and vendor rules
belong to a Family, and every access-control policy scopes to it. Each user gets
one solo Family auto-created at signup (`ensure_default_family()`); their
`is_default` Family is the one they operate on. A `families` row (`id`, `name`).
_Avoid_: household, account

**Family Member**:
A person who belongs to a Family — a `family_members` row (`family_id`,
`user_id`, `role`, `status`, `is_default`). `role ∈ {owner, member}` (the creator
is the `owner`; role is not yet used for authorization). `status ∈ {active,
invited, removed}`, but only `active` rows exist until Invitations ship. A member
is identified for display by their primary email (from `auth.users`), which the
client reads only through the `get_family_members()` `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC.
_Avoid_: user, member, participant

**Receipt**:
A record of a single purchase (merchant, amount, date). May originate from an
uploaded image or be entered by hand. Each Receipt maps to exactly one Expense.
_Avoid_: bill, purchase

**Manual Receipt**:
A Receipt a person creates by typing merchant, amount, and date rather than
uploading an image. It has no image and is not run through OCR; the person is
asserting the details — including the date — directly.
_Avoid_: manual entry, hand receipt

**Expense**:
The categorized view of a Receipt used for reporting. Derived one-to-one from a
Receipt — never stored on its own. Talk about Expenses when reporting or
categorizing; talk about Receipts when capturing.
_Avoid_: cost, spend

**Area of Importance**:
The top tier of the spending hierarchy — e.g. Essential, Priorities, Other. A
family-scoped `importance_areas` row with a `sort_order`. Attaches to the
**Grouping**, not to individual categories, so a Grouping has exactly one
Importance.
_Avoid_: priority band, tier

**Grouping**:
The middle tier of the spending hierarchy — e.g. Everyday, Home, Transportation.
A family-scoped `category_groups` row that belongs to one **Area of Importance**
and gathers many Categories. A Category with no Grouping is _Uncategorized_.

_Avoid_: pivot table, summary

**Spending Chart**:
The charted form of the **Spending Report**: stacked bars (one per Grouping,
stacked by month) with drilldown to Categories — the `/spending` "Chart" view.
_Avoid_: graph, dashboard

**Transaction**:
A line of activity imported from a bank or credit-card statement, reconciled
against Receipts. Distinct from a Receipt: it comes from the bank, not the user.
_Avoid_: charge, payment

**Split Receipt**:
A partial-amount Receipt carved off another. A split is a FULL Receipt record
(not a line-item or child), preserving the 1:1 Receipt↔Expense invariant so no
query or reconciliation code needs to change. Peers share a nullable, indexed
`split_group_id` (UUID). Created by an atomic insert-then-update — the new split
is inserted first, the original reduced second; if the update fails the split is
deleted (best-effort rollback). Both the original's and the split's
`matched_transaction_id` are cleared. Each split takes an optional per-split date
override (deferred charges: hotel/AirBnB/installments) and recomputes
`suspicious_date` from its own date. Splits share the original
`receipt_image_path` — no file is duplicated.
_Avoid_: line item, child receipt

**Source File**:
What a person hands the app — a camera photo, a screenshot, a HEIC picked from
Photos, an attachment on a forwarded email. Transient: it is never stored. Only
its name survives, sanitized into `original_filename`, so people recognize the
receipt by the name they gave it. Its size and format are the app's problem to
absorb, not the person's.
_Avoid_: upload, original, the image

**Receipt Image**:
The single JPEG derived from a **Source File** and stored at
`receipt_image_path` — the only image artifact the app keeps for a Receipt. It
is always JPEG: HEIC and PNG are transcoded on the way in. A PDF receipt is
stored unmodified and is therefore **not** a Receipt Image, which is why it has
no zoom. **Split Receipt** peers share one Receipt Image.
_Avoid_: photo, scan, original, attachment

**Potential Duplicate**:
Two or more Receipts that may record the same purchase — a suspicion raised by
the app, never an assertion. Always _potential_: a family can legitimately hold
two Receipts for the same merchant, amount and day. Duplicate-ness is a property
of a **pair** of Receipts, not of one Receipt, and it is derived on demand rather
than recorded. There is currently no way for a person to settle the suspicion.
_Avoid_: duplicate (unqualified), copy, repeat

## Invariants

**Family-scoped migration invariants**:
When categories and vendor rules moved from user- to family-scope, duplicates
were deduped keeping the FIRST-created row per key; the losing rows' receipt
categorizations become uncategorized via `expense_categories`
`ON DELETE SET NULL`. Category names are unique per family, case-insensitive
(`unique_category_per_family` on `(family_id, LOWER(name))`); vendor patterns are
unique per `(family_id, vendor_pattern)`. Every family-scoped RLS policy requires
`family_members.status = 'active'`. These migrations do not roll back cleanly —
fix forward.

**Foreign-currency reconciliation**:
A Receipt's `total_amount` stays in its ORIGINAL currency; `exchange_rate_to_cad`
is stored on the Receipt at save time (fetched once, never during
reconciliation). Reconciliation matches CAD receipts within a $0.01 tolerance but
foreign-currency receipts within 5% — rate approximation, the ~FX fee, and
settlement timing all move the number. Rates come from the Bank of Canada Valet
API (series `FXEURCAD`, `FXUSDCAD`, `FXGBPCAD`).

**Transaction import dedup**:
Count-based so legitimate in-file repeats survive: for each match key it inserts
`max(0, fileCount − dbCount)` rows, which makes re-import idempotent. The match
key is scoped per family + `credit_card_type`. Excluded rows deliberately count
toward the DB total, so re-importing does not resurrect them.

**Suspicious-date authority**:
Only OCR/automated extraction sets `suspicious_date`. Manual create and any manual
date edit always CLEAR it — user intent is authoritative. Saving through the
receipt edit modal is the confirmation action; there is no separate "confirm
date".

**Suspicious-date scope**:
A suspicious date is a statement that the Receipt's date is untrustworthy, so
that date cannot also be used to decide whether the Receipt is in scope. Counting
or filtering flagged Receipts by the date window would hide exactly the ones
whose date is wrong — they have been filed into the wrong window. The flag is
therefore family-global, deliberately, even while the list beneath it is
date-filtered. Contrast **Split Receipt** grouping, where `split_group_id` is a
trustworthy stored fact and can be resolved globally with no such tension.

**Size limits govern the Receipt Image, not the Source File**:
The 5MB image / 10MB PDF limits state what the family agrees to _store_ — they
describe the **Receipt Image**. A **Source File** is bounded only by a 25MB
ceiling, and that ceiling exists solely to stop an enormous file from exhausting
memory during decode; it is not a statement about acceptable receipts. Asking a
person to shrink a photo the app is about to shrink anyway is asking them to do
the code's job. See [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md).

**Zoom never invents pixels**:
In the receipt viewer 100% means fit-to-viewport, not 1:1, so the zoom ceiling is
a property of the individual image rather than a fixed percentage: it stops at
that image's own natural resolution. Two consequences are deliberate. Zoom
disables itself entirely for an image already at or below viewport size — if
there are no more real pixels there is no more zoom, and a greyed-out control
says so honestly. And storage holds three generations of Receipt Image
(full-resolution from before resizing existed, 2000px, and 2400px), each of
which gets a correct ceiling from its own dimensions with no migration.

**Every uploaded image becomes JPEG**:
HEIC and PNG are transcoded during resize; only PDFs pass through untouched. One
stored format means one set of rules for OCR, display, and storage accounting.
Resizing happens in the browser via Canvas, so this holds only for the upload
path — a receipt arriving by email is stored exactly as it was sent, at whatever
size and format the sender's mail client produced.

**Receipt minimum-data rule**:
A Receipt may be saved with empty fields, but at least ONE of merchant / amount /
date must be non-empty.

**Expense categorization precedence**:
Manual category assignments are never overwritten by auto (vendor-rule)
assignments — auto-categorization only touches uncategorized expenses. New
families get 43 default categories.

I've read the codebase. Facts I'm working from, so I don't ask you about them:

- `receipts` has no note-like column today (`supabase/migrations/20260726120000_baseline.sql:595`). Nothing in the schema or `Receipt.ts` is close.
- Expenses are a derived 1:1 view of receipts (`ExpenseService.ts:22`), so a column on `receipts` is automatically available to both pages — the only work on the expenses side is adding it to the `Expense` projection.
- `ReceiptEditModal.svelte` is shared by the Receipts tab **and** the Reconciliation tab (its own header comment says so, line 17).
- There's a second write surface I suspect you've forgotten: the inline **manual receipt create** form on the receipts page (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:666`, `manualReceipt.ts`).
- Both list pages use `DataTable` with an explicit `columns` array (`receipts/+page.svelte:908`, `expenses/+page.svelte:1220`).
- `docs/domain-model.md` has no term for this concept yet.

Now the grilling. One at a time.

---

**Question 1 — Whose voice is this field?**

You wrote "for now it will only be entered by the user." That "for now" is doing a lot of work, and it decides the schema.

Two futures are plausible from what's already in the repo: OCR could stash something ("couldn't read the tax line"), or reconciliation could ("auto-matched to TD txn 4471"). If either ever lands, a single free-text column becomes a place where a machine can silently overwrite what a person typed.

| Option | Shape | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Human-only field, permanently** | `receipts.notes text` — the app writes it only from a form a person filled in | Zero. If a system message is ever needed, it gets its *own* field, because it's a different concept. |
| **B. Shared field, source-tagged now** | `notes text` + `notes_source` | Pays today for a maybe. |
| **C. Annotation table** | `receipt_notes` rows with author, timestamp, body | Real cost; buys per-member threaded notes. |

**My recommendation: A** — and I'd make it a stated invariant rather than an accident. "This is what a person wrote" is a genuinely different concept from "this is what the app inferred," and the repo already keeps those apart (`suspicious_date` is the app's suspicion; the domain model explicitly says manual entry *clears* it because "user intent is authoritative"). A machine-written note wants a different name, different display, and different edit rules — it should never share this column.

Do you agree the field is human-authored by definition, or do you want to keep the door open for the app writing into it?
1. If the AI writes it will only be at upload or receipt scan time. Since that is before the end user has access to the receipt it doesn't matter.

Understood — the ordering makes it safe: the app may seed the note at capture, and from the moment a person can see it, it's theirs. One column, no source tag. That ordering is the invariant worth writing down (a machine write after a human has seen the receipt would be the bug).

**Question 2 — When a receipt is split, does the note come with it?**

`buildSplitReceiptInsert` (`ReceiptService.ts:598`) is an explicit whitelist — every field is named. So this isn't a default I can fall into; someone has to decide, and if we say nothing the split silently gets a blank note. (Worth knowing: `original_filename` is *already* omitted there, so a split loses its filename today. Same class of decision, made silently.)

The answer depends on what a note is *about*, which is the real question:

- **About the purchase** — "birthday gift for Sam", "reimbursable, client dinner". A $200 hotel bill split into two months: both halves are still the same trip. → **copy**.
- **About the paperwork** — "OCR got the tax wrong, corrected by hand", "second photo, first one was blurry". → **don't copy**; it describes the original artifact.
- **About the split itself** — "this is the deferred January portion". Only meaningful post-split, so neither copy nor blank helps; it wants typing after the fact.

**My recommendation: copy the note to the split.** The domain model already frames a Split Receipt as "a FULL Receipt record" that inherits the original's identity — merchant, card, currency, image all carry over, and the doc's stated goal is that splits need no special-casing anywhere. A note that says "Sam's birthday" is identity, not paperwork. And copying is the recoverable error: the person opens the split and deletes two sentences. Blanking is the unrecoverable one — they don't know the note was ever there, because the split shows an empty field and nothing hints otherwise.

The cost is duplicated text across peers with no link, so editing one leaves the others stale. I think that's acceptable at this size and honest to the "splits are full receipts" model.

Copy, or leave splits blank?
Copy

Fact for later: `Members can update family receipts` (baseline.sql:1061) — **any active family member can edit any family receipt**. So a note is shared, editable by everyone, last-write-wins, with no author recorded. Consistent with what you chose in Q1; flagging it so it isn't a surprise.

---

**Question 3 — Is a note a short label or a paragraph?**

There's tension in your own brief: **1024 characters** is a solid paragraph, but you want "**a few characters** visible" in the list. If notes really run to 1024 chars, a 40-char preview shows an opening fragment and the list preview earns nothing — you'd open the modal every time anyway.

The answer sets three things at once: the input control, whether newlines are legal, and whether the list preview is worth building.

| | Typical content | Control | Newlines | Preview earns its place? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Short label** (~40–80 chars) | "Sam's birthday gift", "reimbursable — client dinner" | `<input type="text">` | No | Yes — you read the whole thing in the row |
| **B. Paragraph** (up to 1024) | "Split with the Hendersons, they owe $42, ask at the BBQ" | `<textarea>`, 3–4 rows | Yes | Marginal — a truncated first line |
| **C. Textarea, but expect short** | Same as A in practice, headroom for B | `<textarea>` | Yes | Yes, most of the time |

**My recommendation: C.** Keep 1024 as the ceiling — it costs nothing, and the one time someone needs to write out a whole story about a warranty claim, the field shouldn't fight them. But use a `<textarea>` rather than an `<input>`, because a single-line input for something people will occasionally paste a paragraph into is miserable to edit (no wrapping, scroll-by-cursor). Allow newlines in storage, and collapse them to spaces *in the preview only*.

The thing I'd rule out is A's hard 80-char cap. A cap that low turns "record details about the receipt" into "record a tag", and you'll hit it on the first genuinely interesting receipt.

Which shape — and is 1024 the number you actually want, or was the `?` in your brief genuine uncertainty?
C

Taking 1024 as settled, then — C keeps it as the ceiling.

---

**Question 4 — How is the 1024 enforced, and what happens when someone hits it?**

Two sub-decisions that get conflated. First, *where* the limit lives:

The gate needs a DB `CHECK (char_length(notes) <= 1024)` regardless — it's one line, and it's the only guarantee that holds for write paths that don't go through the modal. There are already three such paths (email ingestion in `supabase/functions/`, `ExpenseImportService`, and the OCR seeding you described in Q1), and any of them could grow a note-writing branch later.

Second, and more interesting — *what the textarea does at 1024*:

| Option | Behaviour | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|
| **A. `maxlength="1024"`** | Browser stops accepting input; a paste over the limit is **silently chopped** | Person pastes 1500 chars, sees text, saves, never learns 476 chars vanished |
| **B. Counter + blocked Save** | Type/paste freely; counter appears near the limit, turns red past it; Save disabled with an inline message | Person must trim it themselves |
| **C. Both** | `maxlength` plus a counter | Counter never fires — `maxlength` makes exceeding it impossible |

**My recommendation: B, no `maxlength`.** Silent truncation on paste is the one failure here you cannot detect after the fact — the receipt looks fine, the note reads as complete, and the last sentence is gone. B makes the person the one who decides what to cut. The modal already has the machinery: an `error` state rendered at the top of the body (line 236) and a save-time validation precedent in `hasMinimumData` (line 128).

One detail I'll just handle rather than ask about: JS `.length` counts UTF-16 units while Postgres `char_length` counts characters, so an emoji is 2 to the browser and 1 to the DB. That skews *conservative* — the client will never let through something the DB rejects — so no special handling is needed.

content.text:
**Question 6 — This is the important one. The Expenses page will erase notes, and it's already erasing other things.**

`src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte:524` builds a *synthetic* `ReceiptRow` from the `Expense` projection, hard-coding the fields `Expense` doesn't carry:

```
tax: null,
credit_card_name: null,
credit_card_last_4: null,
matched_transaction_id: null,   // ← Expense DOES carry this; it's discarded anyway
suspicious_date: false,
```

…and then `handleReceiptSave` (line 550) writes every one of those back to the database (lines 559–566).

**So today: open any receipt from the Expenses page, change nothing, click Save — and you erase its tax amount, card name, last-4 digits, and its reconciliation match.** A receipt matched to a TD transaction becomes unmatched. That is a pre-existing bug, not something I'm introducing, and I'll log it in `docs/product-backlog.md` either way.

It matters here because `notes` lands in exactly the same trap: the expenses page would synthesize `notes: null` and the first save from that page silently destroys what someone typed. Since you want the note *visible* on the expenses page, people will click that row precisely because they saw the note.

| Option | What happens | 
|---|---|
| **A. Fix the root cause** — expenses page fetches the real receipt row before opening the modal | Notes safe; tax/card/match bug fixed for free. Needs a `getById` on `ReceiptService` (doesn't exist yet — only `list`) and one extra round-trip on row click. |
| **B. Add `notes` to the `Expense` projection and thread it through** | Notes safe. Tax, card, and match keep getting erased. Widens the synthetic-row pattern that caused this. |
| **C. Ship notes, log the bug, don't touch it** | Notes get erased from the expenses page. Not viable given B5. |

**My recommendation: A.** The synthetic row is the defect — it's a `ReceiptRow`-shaped object that isn't one, and every field added to `receipts` from now on inherits the bug. Fetching the real row deletes the whole class. It also removes work: no `notes` in the `Expense` interface, no change to `ExpenseService.getExpenses`'s select…

…**except** that B5 needs the note in the list rows to render the preview, so `Expense` needs `notes` regardless. Fine — but then `notes` on `Expense` is a *display* projection, and the modal gets its data from the fetch, not from the synthesized row.

Also flagging: `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (line 118) is an allow-list. Miss `notes` there and saves silently no-op — no error, the field just never persists. Easy to forget; I won't.

Do I fix the expenses-page synthetic row as part of this work (A), or keep it scoped and accept that the fix lands separately (B)?
A

content.text:
Following that thread turned up something worth a decision. Adding one column to `receipts` means touching **five separately hand-maintained field lists**, none of which the compiler checks:

| # | Location | If you forget `notes` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (`ReceiptService.ts:118`) | Update silently strips it. No error. |
| 2 | patch literal, receipts page (`+page.svelte:218`) | Note never saves from Receipts |
| 3 | patch literal, reconciliation page (`:384`) | Note never saves from Reconciliation |
| 4 | patch literal, expenses page (`:555`) | Note never saves from Expenses |
| 5 | `isDirty` in the modal (`ReceiptEditModal.svelte:68`) | Close a modal with an unsaved note → **no warning, note discarded** |

All five are inferred object literals or string sets, so omitting a field type-checks cleanly. That's how reconciliation's patch ended up missing `suspicious_date` while the receipts page's has it — the two have already drifted (compare line 228 to line 392).

---

**Question 7 — Five lists, or one?**

- **A. Add `notes` to all five by hand.** Smallest diff. Leaves the next person the same five-way trap, and the lists have already proven they drift.
- **B. Extract one `buildReceiptPatch(row)` used by all three pages,** and add `notes` to `#EDITABLE_FIELDS` + `isDirty`. Reduces five to three, and makes the two patch variants' drift an explicit decision rather than an accident.

**My recommendation: B.** The project already has this instinct — `DataTable` (RF-03) was extracted for exactly this reason, and `#EDITABLE_FIELDS` exists because someone hit this before. Three page-level patch literals that must agree, and already don't, is the same problem one layer up.

Caveat, and it's why I'm asking rather than assuming: the reconciliation/receipts drift on `suspicious_date` may be *deliberate* (reconciliation deliberately not confirming a date it isn't showing?). `ReceiptService.update` forces `suspicious_date = false` whenever `transaction_date` is present anyway (line 151), so both pages behave identically in practice and the drift looks vestigial — but I'd rather you confirm than have me flatten a distinction you meant.

A or B? And do you know of a reason reconciliation's patch deliberately omits `suspicious_date`?

lastPrompt: A

content.text: B

Noted on B. I'll treat the `suspicious_date` drift as vestigial — `update()` forces it to `false` whenever `transaction_date` is present (line 151), so both pages already behave identically — and I'll say so explicitly in the design doc as an assumption rather than a finding.

---

**Question 8 — Does the manual-create form get a note field?**

You said "only editable in the receipts dialog," but there's a second write surface: the inline **manual receipt** form (`receipts/+page.svelte:666`), a collapsed 3-field quick-entry (merchant, amount, date — `manualReceipt.ts`).

The case *for* adding it there is stronger than it first looks: a **Manual Receipt has no image**. For an uploaded receipt, the image holds the detail and the note is supplementary. For a manual one, merchant/amount/date is *everything the app knows* — the note would be the only place any actual detail can live. So manual receipts are arguably where notes matter most.

The case against: Q4 gave notes a real validation story (counter, Save blocked past 1024, inline message). Putting the field on a second surface means implementing that story twice — and Q7 just showed what happens in this codebase when the same thing is maintained in two places. The inline form is also deliberately minimal and collapsed by default; a textarea turns quick-entry into a form.

**My recommendation: A — no note on the create form.** Create, then click the row you just created and add the note in the modal. It's two clicks, the row is right there, and it keeps notes to exactly one write surface with one validation implementation. If manual receipts turn out to be the dominant note-taking case, adding the field later is trivial *because* the validation will already be factored out for reuse.

A (modal only), or B (also on manual create)?
No - just a bit of text

Read as: no note on the manual-create form, and keep the whole thing small. Agreed.

content.text:
`escapeCSVField` (line 148) already quotes commas, quotes **and newlines** — so a multi-line note exports correctly with no new escaping work. And `parseExpenseImportCsv` resolves columns by header name and simply doesn't look up ones it doesn't need, so an extra column can't break re-import.

---

**Question 9 — Do notes appear in the CSV and PDF exports?**

| | Cost | Value |
|---|---|---|
| **CSV** (`CSVExportService`) | ~2 lines: one header entry, one `escapeCSVField(...)` in `buildRow` (line 79). Escaping is already correct. | High for the case people actually write notes for — "reimbursable", "client dinner", "warranty until 2028". That's the column you want when handing a file to an accountant. |
| **PDF summary table** (`PDFExportService`) | Real work. Fixed column x-positions (line 49) on an already-tight per-category table, plus wrapping a paragraph into a row. | Low — it's a spend roll-up, not a detail report. |
| **PDF per-receipt page** | Cheap — one line under the existing reference header (line 470/506), which already prints "Merchant — Date — Amount". | Moderate. That page is where you're looking at the receipt itself. |

**My recommendation: CSV yes, both PDF paths no.** The CSV is the machine-readable extract — the format whose whole job is to carry the data somewhere else — and leaving a field out of it means the export quietly isn't a full extract any more. Two lines, no escaping risk, and re-import is unaffected.

The PDF is a *presentation* of spending, and both PDF options are layout work in service of a field you've described as "just a bit of text." The per-receipt page is the one I'd revisit first if you ever want it.

The one thing I'd flag: adding a 5th column changes a file the family may already have spreadsheets pointed at. It's appended at the end, so formulas keyed on columns A–D are unaffected — but it is a change you didn't ask for, so say if you'd rather leave the export alone.
