content.content:
1	# Backlog
2	
3	The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
4	refactoring. Everything here is **open**: something a person could pick up.
5	
6	**Completed work is deleted from this file, not annotated.** History lives in git,
7	in [ADRs](adr/) for decisions and rejected paths, in [`prd-done/`](prd-done/) for
8	finished PRDs, and in `CLAUDE.md` for anything that stays true and will bite
9	someone later. When an item lands, salvage any durable lesson into one of those
10	and remove the bullet. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the
11	full detail lives in [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a
12	reference, not a separate to-do list.
13	
14	## Features
15	
16	- **Spending Report — remaining slices.** The report ships: table + chart views, cell drill-down, editable hierarchy, assign-on-create, and historical-expense import are all live. Still open, roughly in priority order: **chart-bar drill-down** (the same drill affordance the table cells have — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); **prior-period overlay + year-over-year** (unblocked now that historical years can be imported); quarter/period selection; multi-chart menu; export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
17	- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
18	- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account. This interacts with the unverified-alias security item below — verification is the fix, so design them together.
19	- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped self-insert policy). The read-only half already shipped — the Profile page lists family members via the `get_family_members()` RPC — so what remains is invite / accept / remove.
20	- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). One on-device check is still outstanding: HEIC is now decoded and transcoded to JPEG like everything else (see [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md)), but nobody has confirmed what an iPhone actually hands over, or that Safari decodes it as expected — if it doesn't, the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is now refused rather than silently uploaded full-size.
21	- **Vendor-rule management UI.** Vendor rules are created silently — on first categorization, and (once the design above lands) applied by a database trigger — but **nothing in the app lists them**. There is no way to see which rules exist, correct one, or delete a bad one. Sharpened by the junk-rule item under Correctness below: garbled OCR merchant names create patterns that never match again, and today they are invisible and unremovable.
22	- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y** _(optional UX, low priority)_. A recent-categories section in the dropdown, a mobile-responsive category dropdown, and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support were specced but never built.
23	- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits** _(optional, low priority)_. The read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal.
24	
25	## Bugs / UX issues
26	
27	- **Receipt with no date is hard to find.** If a receipt has no date it is hard to locate in the receipts view.
28	- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
29	- **Split receipts: decide what a split inherits.** Punted 2026-08-03 during the design above. `splitReceipt` copies the original's merchant into a new receipt row, so once the vendor-rule trigger exists a split will get **the merchant's rule** — even when the parent was manually reclassified away from it. That is an unexamined default, not a decision. The alternatives are inheriting the parent's current category (most recent human signal about that purchase) or leaving splits deliberately uncategorized (you split _because_ the halves differ). Needs its own design pass.
30	- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
31	- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
32	- **Needs-review count is global but its list is date-filtered — and the empty state lies.** The badge counts `allReceipts.filter(r => r.suspicious_date)` (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:589`), which is **correct and deliberate**: a receipt whose date OCR'd wrong has been filed into the wrong date window, so scoping the count by that untrusted date is circular (see the "Suspicious-date scope" invariant in [Domain model](domain-model.md)). The defect is that ticking the checkbox still applies the date filter on top (`:327` then `:333`), so the badge promises 12 and the list shows 3. Worst case, when the date filter empties the list the empty state renders **"All dates verified! No receipts need date review"** (`:881`) while receipts are in fact flagged. Options discussed: **(a)** suspend the date filter while needs-review is ticked, so badge count == rows shown, with a visible cue that the range is ignored — this also dissolves the false empty state; **(b)** show a split "3 in range / 12 total"; **(c)** scope the badge to the window — rejected, it hides precisely the mis-dated receipts. Punted 2026-07-26 without picking one.
33	- **Duplicate detection: three inconsistent scopes, no way to dismiss, and it misses OCR date drift.** Three separate problems in one feature on `src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte`. **(1) No dismissal.** Duplicate is derived, never stored — `detectDuplicates()` groups on the composite key `total_amount|transaction_date` (`src/lib/utils/duplicateDetection.ts:14`). An `is_duplicate` column and a `find_duplicate_receipts()` RPC once existed and were dropped (`supabase/migrations-archive/009_remove_duplicate_detection.sql`), so there is nowhere to record "I checked; these are two genuine purchases" and a legitimate pair flags forever. Open modelling question if this is built: dismissal is **pair-scoped** (you asserted A and B are distinct, so a later third copy still flags) vs **receipt-scoped** (mutes the receipt, and so hides the real duplicate when a third copy arrives) — pair-scoped looks right. **(2) Three scopes for one concept.** The row badge and yellow highlight are computed over the date-filtered list (`:396`), while the checkbox filter (`:317`) and the count badge (`:400`) are computed over `allReceipts`. So with a date filter on and the checkbox ticked, a receipt whose only partner sits outside the window is listed with no badge and no highlight; with the checkbox off, that same cross-boundary duplicate is silently invisible. **(3) Match rule is keyed on OCR's weakest field.** Exact `transaction_date` equality, when `resolveOcrReceiptDate` (`src/lib/utils/receiptDateCorrection.ts:186`) can rewrite an implausible date within a 90-day window — two photos of the same receipt can land on different dates and never group. It also ignores `merchant_name` (so $84.32 at Costco and $84.32 at the dentist on one day flag) and ignores `currency` (USD vs CAD same-day flags). Candidate rule: amount exact + date within ±3 days + normalized merchant equal, reusing `ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` (`ExpenseService.ts:321`) and reconciliation's `maxDaysDifference: 3` / `amountTolerance` (`src/lib/models/Reconciliation.ts:29`, `ReconciliationService.ts:369`) rather than inventing thresholds. Note a date _window_ breaks transitivity — A~B and B~C no longer implies A~C — so a "duplicate group" becomes a graph of pairs, an independent argument for pair-scoped dismissal. A file content hash would catch identical re-uploads with perfect precision but does nothing for two separate photos; additive, not a substitute. Punted 2026-07-26.
34	- **Reconciliation split-group badge is window-scoped when it should be global (inverse of the above).** `getSplitGroupInfo` (`src/routes/reconciliation/+page.svelte:529`, called at `:1046`) searches only `displayRows`, which `loadReconciliation()` already restricted to the URL date window. A split group straddling the window boundary collapses to `groupReceipts.length <= 1`, returns `null`, and the "2 of 3" badge silently vanishes — so a partial split looks like an ordinary whole receipt. Unlike the needs-review case, `split_group_id` is a trustworthy stored fact, so it can simply be resolved globally.
35	- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).
36	
37	## Engineering
38	
39	### In progress
40	
41	- **🟢 Bombadil property-based UI testing (spike) — built and running.** `bombadil/transactions.ts` explores `/transactions` against the local stack with 12 properties (the 4 free ones plus a pathname tripwire, filter/counter/selection invariants). Session comes from a DEV-and-loopback-gated auto-login (`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts`); `npm run bombadil` after `npm run db:fresh` + `npm run dev`. A clean 60-second run explores ~390 actions (≈5/sec) with no violations. Open follow-ups: **`PressKey` wedges the run** — every run including it hung with the browser at 100% CPU, so keyboard interaction is excluded entirely and the cause is undiagnosed; **native `<select>` popups hang it too**, so the card/bank-type filter is unexplored (Chrome renders the option list outside the page); **Delete / bulk-delete are excluded** because they use `confirm()`; and **`--reproduce` has never been exercised**. Widening to a second page (which means a second hand-written specification, not a config change) and deciding whether it earns a nightly GitHub Action (`antithesishq/bombadil-action@v2`) are the next questions. See [Bombadil spike handoff](plans-done/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).
42	
43	### Security
44	
45	- **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
46	- **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a _direct_ `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way. Audit every other `SECURITY DEFINER` function for the same hole and revoke explicitly where `authenticated` is the only legitimate caller.
47	- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.
48	
49	### Dependencies
50	
51	- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix — decision needed.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there is no version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx`. Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball via `overrides` — clears the CVEs and keeps `.xls`, but adds a non-registry dep our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`**, so it drops that support unless paired with a BIFF parser. **The decision to make: is legacy `.xls` still required?** Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers practical risk.
52	- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie`. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix`. Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
53	- **🔴 New since the last audit: 6 further `npm audit` findings, 2 of them critical.** _(Surfaced 2026-07-26 while adding the Bombadil dev dependency; none introduced by it — `@antithesishq/bombadil` has zero dependencies. The total is now 9: 2 low, 1 moderate, 4 high, 2 critical.)_ Every one claims a fix via a plain `npm audit fix`, so this is mostly a bump-and-verify job — but it needs the fixes actually applied and the suites re-run, not just logged.
54	  - **CRITICAL — `@vitest/browser <=3.2.6`:** Browser Mode provider commands bypass the file-access permission gate ([GHSA-p63j-vcc4-9vmv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p63j-vcc4-9vmv)). Two advisories, counted against both `@vitest/browser` and `vitest`. We run browser-mode tests, so this is the one to fix first.
55	  - **MODERATE — `@sveltejs/kit <=2.70.1`:** prototype pollution in the remote-function form file-input deletion path ([GHSA-866w-xmhq-wj7x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-866w-xmhq-wj7x)), plus a Node crash on large remote-form payloads ([GHSA-wqjv-9729-c5q2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wqjv-9729-c5q2)). We don't use remote functions today, but this is shipped framework code.
56	  - **HIGH — `postcss <=8.5.17`:** path traversal via `sourceMappingURL` auto-loading discloses arbitrary `.map` files ([GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849)).
57	  - **HIGH — `js-yaml 4.0.0–4.2.0`:** merge-key chains force quadratic CPU ([GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m)). Build-time only.
58	  - **HIGH — `brace-expansion <=5.0.7`:** exponential-time expansion and unbounded expansion length ([GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp), [GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg)). Transitive via glob/eslint; build-time only.
59	
60	### Correctness / infrastructure
61	
62	- **Stack-dependent suites are still outside the gate.** The build gate (`vercel.json` → `npm run verify`) covers `check`, `check:deno`, `lint`, and the node-side Vitest project; the `client` browser project runs advisory-only in GitHub Actions. `test:e2e` and `test:integration` need a live Supabase stack and run nowhere automatically. Decide whether they earn a scheduled job — that is also the natural home for the service-drift check below.
63	- **The RLS integration suite un-skips on an env var, and would then break the gate.** `family-category-visibility.spec.ts` sits in the `server` Vitest project, so `npm run verify` collects it every run; it skips only because `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is unset. Add that key to Vercel's build environment (an easy thing to do for an unrelated reason) and the 8 tests flip from skipped to failing with `TypeError: fetch failed` — no Postgres is reachable from a build container — and every deploy is blocked with a misleading error. Same trap locally for anyone who exports the key. Options: move the suite out of the `server` project into its own Vitest project that `verify` doesn't run, or make the skip condition an explicit opt-in flag (`RUN_RLS_TESTS=1`) rather than the incidental presence of a credential. Documented for now in [local-dev.md](local-dev.md#testing).
64	- **`receipts.family_id` is nullable, but a Receipt must always belong to a Family.** The intended invariant is that a Receipt cannot exist without a `family_id`; the schema does not enforce it. The column is declared `"family_id" "uuid"` with no `NOT NULL` (baseline `:607`, confirmed live as `is_nullable = YES`), and `receipts_family_id_fkey` is **`ON DELETE SET NULL`** (`:946`) — so deleting a Family silently orphans its Receipts rather than being prevented or cascading. All four receipts RLS policies then carry an explicit `family_id IS NULL → fall back to owner (user_id)` branch (`:1021` insert, `:1049` delete, `:1061` update, `:1073` select), so an orphan reverts to owner-private and disappears for every other family member. **`expense_categories` has no such fallback** — its policy joins `receipts r → family_members fm ON fm.family_id = r.family_id` (`:1151`), so an orphaned Receipt's category row becomes invisible and unmanageable to _everyone, including its owner_. That inconsistency is the sharpest symptom. The nullability also propagates into application types (`InsertedReceiptRow` in `ReceiptService.ts:41`, and the receipts entry in `src/lib/tests/builders/testDatabase.ts`) and into the `apply_vendor_rule_after_insert` trigger, which skips rows whose `family_id` is null. Fixing it: **decide family-deletion semantics first** — `RESTRICT` (block deleting a Family that still owns Receipts) is safer than `CASCADE` (deleting a Family destroys its Receipts and their stored files). Then backfill any existing NULLs, `SET NOT NULL`, replace the FK action, drop the `IS NULL` branches from the four policies, and simplify the types. One case needs a deliberate answer: `set_receipt_family_id` (`:387`) fills the column from `ensure_default_family()`, which **can return null** — under `NOT NULL` that insert would fail loudly instead of silently producing an orphan, which is probably correct but is a behaviour change for any path where the user has no default family.
65	- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (originally `003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, carried into the baseline). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path — they survive only if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback. Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert in a new migration and confirm the remote function matches.
66	- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That is the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by reading the year in a **`+page.ts` `load`** (`data.year`) with the arrows using **`goto`** — `load` re-runs with the right URL on every navigation. (Client-side derivation did NOT hold up: both `$app/stores` `$page` and the `$app/state` reactive `page` went stale on Back.) Apply the same `load`-based pattern here, and audit any other `$derived(… $page.url …)` site. Latent — not yet reproduced for expenses.
67	- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle was specced but never built. **Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.**
68	- **Local Supabase service versions drift silently from production.** `supabase/.temp/*-version` records the remote project's service versions **as of the last `supabase link`** and `supabase start` runs exactly those images, so local mirrors whatever prod looked like at link time. Supabase keeps upgrading the hosted project; local never moves. The pins sat at 2025-11-27 for eight months, leaving local on `gotrue v2.183.0` / `storage-api v1.31.1` against prod's `v2.193.1` / `v1.67.15` — i.e. we develop and test auth and storage, the two services `receipts` signed-URL security rests on, against versions prod stopped running long ago. `supabase start` printed the warning on every single start; nobody reads a warning in a 15-line startup log. Fixed for now by re-linking (see [Local development](local-dev.md)), but it will re-open. **Detection is scriptable:** read the four `.temp/*-version` files and diff against the `remote` field of `supabase services --output json`. Do _not_ diff against that command's `local` field — that reports the CLI's bundled defaults, not what is actually running, and yields permanent false positives. Best home is a scheduled job once CI exists; a local pre-`db:up` check would be per-developer and easy to ignore.
69	- **`adapter-auto` leaves the deploy target implicit.** `svelte.config.js` still uses the scaffold default, which infers the adapter from build-time env vars — on Vercel that resolves to `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel`. It works, and nothing is broken. But the choice of Node vs Edge runtime, region, and per-route function config is currently whatever the auto-detect picks, which matters for the long-running Mistral OCR calls. Pin `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel` explicitly when convenient and set the runtime deliberately. Low priority.
70	- **`allowScripts` is stale for `esbuild` — install scripts are being blocked.** `npm ci` warns: `esbuild@0.28.1 (postinstall: node install.js)` is not covered by the `allowScripts` map in `package.json`, which still lists only `esbuild@0.27.7`. Two esbuild copies exist in the lockfile — `0.27.7` at the root (used by Vite/Vitest, approved) and `0.28.1` nested under `tsx` (not approved). The current CI job is unaffected because `npm run verify` never invokes `tsx`, but the `seed:demo` scripts do. Either approve `esbuild@0.28.1` or confirm the nested copy works without its postinstall.
71	- **Watch for storage-policy drift.** `supabase db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are hand-maintained at the end of `20260726120000_baseline.sql`. A future storage change written only as a migration will be lost the next time the baseline is regenerated; one made only in the dashboard will never reach a new environment. Consider a check that diffs live storage policies against the baseline.
72	- **Emailed receipts are never resized — the two capture paths store different things.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes straight to storage (`supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts:137`) with no size check and no resize, so a receipt forwarded by email is stored at whatever size the sender's mail client produced, while the same receipt uploaded in the browser becomes a 2400px JPEG. Deliberate for now — it is a Deno edge function with no Canvas, so matching it means a WASM image library plus a second copy of the resize rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/` kept in lock-step by hand (the burden CLAUDE.md already flags for the date-correction code), and CPU time inside a webhook that must answer quickly. Recorded as an accepted asymmetry in [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) and the ["Every uploaded image becomes JPEG" invariant](domain-model.md). Revisit if storage cost or emailed-receipt volume grows.
73	- **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
74	- **`ReceiptService` ships debug logging to production.** Three `console.log`s on the receipts-page load path (`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:84`, `:91`, `:101`) print the user id, the **full `family_members` rows for that user**, and the fetched receipt payload to the browser console on every visit. The middle one is a query run purely to log its result — it is labelled "for debugging" and nothing consumes it. A fourth logs every created receipt in `insertReceiptOrCleanupUpload` (`:347`); it is the only remaining reader of `family_id` on `InsertedReceiptRow`, so deleting it may let that type collapse back to `ReceiptRow`. Delete the logs and the debug query.
75	- **Receipts page fetches every family expense just to colour one column.** `loadCategories` (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:254`) calls `ExpenseService.getExpenses` — a full paged pass over `receipts` with an embed — solely to build `categoryMap` for the edit modal. Adding the Category column (see [Classify on the Receipts page](plans/2026-08-03-classify-on-receipts-page-design.md)) puts that second full-table read on the render path, on a page that has already loaded every receipt once. It should read `expense_categories` for the receipts already in hand instead.
76	- **Garbled OCR merchant names create junk and orphaned vendor rules.** `ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` (`:321`) only lowercases and strips punctuation, so store numbers survive: `"STARBUCKS #1234"` becomes the pattern `starbucks 1234`, which will never match another receipt. The Receipts Category column makes this worse by design — it is the fast path, so people will categorize from the list _before_ opening the modal to clean up the merchant name, and fixing the name afterwards orphans the rule that was just created against the old one. Needs a normalization rule that drops trailing store/terminal numbers, and pairs with the vendor-rule management UI under Features (today these rules are invisible and unremovable).
77	- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for the nothing-found-anywhere row, but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case. The tests assert the real `422`; the PRD table is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the table or leave the note.
78	
79	## Refactoring
80	
81	Every catalogued refactoring (**RF-01→13**, plus code-review follow-ups
82	**RV-01→11**) has landed — see [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md) for the
83	per-item Landed notes. The only other outstanding entries are the two deferred
84	value-object questions, **RF-D1** (`Money`) and **RF-D2** (typed date) — both a
85	recorded _keep-primitives_ decision, not scheduled work. New refactoring ideas start
86	here as one-liners and get promoted to an `RF-NN` entry only when work begins.
87	
88	- **Delete the dead `#{#...}` spec tags.** `src/` carries **649** traceability tags
89	  (**179** distinct, across **64** files) of the form `#{#exp2a}`, `#{#vca5a}`,
90	  `#{#rmc2a}` — plus prose headers naming files like
91	  `specs/specifications/expense-categorization.md`. **That directory does not exist**:
92	  it was deleted deliberately in `92e9ae1` ("Kill off specs", 2026-07-06), and
93	  `CLAUDE.md` does not list the tags as a convention. Every one is now a reference to
94	  nothing, and they cost real time — tracing `#{#vca2a}` to its (non-existent) source
95	  took several minutes during the Receipts categorization work. They also **propagate**:
96	  the convention is invisible-but-contagious, so anyone editing tagged code copies the
97	  tags into new code, as happened in that change. Worse, deleting tagged code can strand
98	  a tag on its last remaining reference — `#{#vca2a}` briefly survived only on a comment
99	  explaining that the behaviour it named no longer happened there. A sweep is
100	  mechanical (regex-removable) but touches 64 files, so it wants its own commit and its
101	  own review, and should land alongside a `CLAUDE.md` note so the convention is not
102	  reintroduced. Decide first whether any tag is still load-bearing — grep suggests not,
103	  since nothing resolves them.
104	
105	## Open questions
106	
107	- **Combining receipts for one expense.** How to handle when two receipts should be combined into one expense to match — e.g. two medications picked up at the same time.
108	- **WealthSimple refund handling.** WealthSimple records several rows when a refund is issued. Example:
109	
110	  ```csv
111	  "2026-05-24","2026-05-24","Refund initiated","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
112	  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","33.9","CAD"
113	  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
114	  ```

# Backlog

The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
refactoring. Everything here is **open**: something a person could pick up.

**Completed work is deleted from this file, not annotated.** History lives in git,
in [ADRs](adr/) for decisions and rejected paths, in [`prd-done/`](prd-done/) for
finished PRDs, and in `CLAUDE.md` for anything that stays true and will bite
someone later. When an item lands, salvage any durable lesson into one of those
and remove the bullet. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the
full detail lives in [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a
reference, not a separate to-do list.

## Features

- **Spending Report — remaining slices.** The report ships: table + chart views, cell drill-down, editable hierarchy, assign-on-create, and historical-expense import are all live. Still open, roughly in priority order: **chart-bar drill-down** (the same drill affordance the table cells have — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); **prior-period overlay + year-over-year** (unblocked now that historical years can be imported); quarter/period selection; multi-chart menu; export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account. This interacts with the unverified-alias security item below — verification is the fix, so design them together.
- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped self-insert policy). The read-only half already shipped — the Profile page lists family members via the `get_family_members()` RPC — so what remains is invite / accept / remove.
- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). One on-device check is still outstanding: HEIC is now decoded and transcoded to JPEG like everything else (see [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md)), but nobody has confirmed what an iPhone actually hands over, or that Safari decodes it as expected — if it doesn't, the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is now refused rather than silently uploaded full-size.
- **Vendor-rule management UI.** Vendor rules are created silently — on first categorization, and (once the design above lands) applied by a database trigger — but **nothing in the app lists them**. There is no way to see which rules exist, correct one, or delete a bad one. Sharpened by the junk-rule item under Correctness below: garbled OCR merchant names create patterns that never match again, and today they are invisible and unremovable.
- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y** _(optional UX, low priority)_. A recent-categories section in the dropdown, a mobile-responsive category dropdown, and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support were specced but never built.
- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits** _(optional, low priority)_. The read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal.

## Bugs / UX issues

- **Receipt with no date is hard to find.** If a receipt has no date it is hard to locate in the receipts view.
- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
- **Split receipts: decide what a split inherits.** Punted 2026-08-03 during the design above. `splitReceipt` copies the original's merchant into a new receipt row, so once the vendor-rule trigger exists a split will get **the merchant's rule** — even when the parent was manually reclassified away from it. That is an unexamined default, not a decision. The alternatives are inheriting the parent's current category (most recent human signal about that purchase) or leaving splits deliberately uncategorized (you split _because_ the halves differ). Needs its own design pass.
- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
- **Needs-review count is global but its list is date-filtered — and the empty state lies.** The badge counts `allReceipts.filter(r => r.suspicious_date)` (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:589`), which is **correct and deliberate**: a receipt whose date OCR'd wrong has been filed into the wrong date window, so scoping the count by that untrusted date is circular (see the "Suspicious-date scope" invariant in [Domain model](domain-model.md)). The defect is that ticking the checkbox still applies the date filter on top (`:327` then `:333`), so the badge promises 12 and the list shows 3. Worst case, when the date filter empties the list the empty state renders **"All dates verified! No receipts need date review"** (`:881`) while receipts are in fact flagged. Options discussed: **(a)** suspend the date filter while needs-review is ticked, so badge count == rows shown, with a visible cue that the range is ignored — this also dissolves the false empty state; **(b)** show a split "3 in range / 12 total"; **(c)** scope the badge to the window — rejected, it hides precisely the mis-dated receipts. Punted 2026-07-26 without picking one.
- **Duplicate detection: three inconsistent scopes, no way to dismiss, and it misses OCR date drift.** Three separate problems in one feature on `src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte`. **(1) No dismissal.** Duplicate is derived, never stored — `detectDuplicates()` groups on the composite key `total_amount|transaction_date` (`src/lib/utils/duplicateDetection.ts:14`). An `is_duplicate` column and a `find_duplicate_receipts()` RPC once existed and were dropped (`supabase/migrations-archive/009_remove_duplicate_detection.sql`), so there is nowhere to record "I checked; these are two genuine purchases" and a legitimate pair flags forever. Open modelling question if this is built: dismissal is **pair-scoped** (you asserted A and B are distinct, so a later third copy still flags) vs **receipt-scoped** (mutes the receipt, and so hides the real duplicate when a third copy arrives) — pair-scoped looks right. **(2) Three scopes for one concept.** The row badge and yellow highlight are computed over the date-filtered list (`:396`), while the checkbox filter (`:317`) and the count badge (`:400`) are computed over `allReceipts`. So with a date filter on and the checkbox ticked, a receipt whose only partner sits outside the window is listed with no badge and no highlight; with the checkbox off, that same cross-boundary duplicate is silently invisible. **(3) Match rule is keyed on OCR's weakest field.** Exact `transaction_date` equality, when `resolveOcrReceiptDate` (`src/lib/utils/receiptDateCorrection.ts:186`) can rewrite an implausible date within a 90-day window — two photos of the same receipt can land on different dates and never group. It also ignores `merchant_name` (so $84.32 at Costco and $84.32 at the dentist on one day flag) and ignores `currency` (USD vs CAD same-day flags). Candidate rule: amount exact + date within ±3 days + normalized merchant equal, reusing `ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` (`ExpenseService.ts:321`) and reconciliation's `maxDaysDifference: 3` / `amountTolerance` (`src/lib/models/Reconciliation.ts:29`, `ReconciliationService.ts:369`) rather than inventing thresholds. Note a date _window_ breaks transitivity — A~B and B~C no longer implies A~C — so a "duplicate group" becomes a graph of pairs, an independent argument for pair-scoped dismissal. A file content hash would catch identical re-uploads with perfect precision but does nothing for two separate photos; additive, not a substitute. Punted 2026-07-26.
- **Reconciliation split-group badge is window-scoped when it should be global (inverse of the above).** `getSplitGroupInfo` (`src/routes/reconciliation/+page.svelte:529`, called at `:1046`) searches only `displayRows`, which `loadReconciliation()` already restricted to the URL date window. A split group straddling the window boundary collapses to `groupReceipts.length <= 1`, returns `null`, and the "2 of 3" badge silently vanishes — so a partial split looks like an ordinary whole receipt. Unlike the needs-review case, `split_group_id` is a trustworthy stored fact, so it can simply be resolved globally.
- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).

## Engineering

### In progress

- **🟢 Bombadil property-based UI testing (spike) — built and running.** `bombadil/transactions.ts` explores `/transactions` against the local stack with 12 properties (the 4 free ones plus a pathname tripwire, filter/counter/selection invariants). Session comes from a DEV-and-loopback-gated auto-login (`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts`); `npm run bombadil` after `npm run db:fresh` + `npm run dev`. A clean 60-second run explores ~390 actions (≈5/sec) with no violations. Open follow-ups: **`PressKey` wedges the run** — every run including it hung with the browser at 100% CPU, so keyboard interaction is excluded entirely and the cause is undiagnosed; **native `<select>` popups hang it too**, so the card/bank-type filter is unexplored (Chrome renders the option list outside the page); **Delete / bulk-delete are excluded** because they use `confirm()`; and **`--reproduce` has never been exercised**. Widening to a second page (which means a second hand-written specification, not a config change) and deciding whether it earns a nightly GitHub Action (`antithesishq/bombadil-action@v2`) are the next questions. See [Bombadil spike handoff](plans-done/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).

### Security

- **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
- **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a _direct_ `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way. Audit every other `SECURITY DEFINER` function for the same hole and revoke explicitly where `authenticated` is the only legitimate caller.
- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.

### Dependencies

- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix — decision needed.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there is no version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx`. Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball via `overrides` — clears the CVEs and keeps `.xls`, but adds a non-registry dep our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`**, so it drops that support unless paired with a BIFF parser. **The decision to make: is legacy `.xls` still required?** Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers practical risk.
- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie`. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix`. Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
- **🔴 New since the last audit: 6 further `npm audit` findings, 2 of them critical.** _(Surfaced 2026-07-26 while adding the Bombadil dev dependency; none introduced by it — `@antithesishq/bombadil` has zero dependencies. The total is now 9: 2 low, 1 moderate, 4 high, 2 critical.)_ Every one claims a fix via a plain `npm audit fix`, so this is mostly a bump-and-verify job — but it needs the fixes actually applied and the suites re-run, not just logged.
  - **CRITICAL — `@vitest/browser <=3.2.6`:** Browser Mode provider commands bypass the file-access permission gate ([GHSA-p63j-vcc4-9vmv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p63j-vcc4-9vmv)). Two advisories, counted against both `@vitest/browser` and `vitest`. We run browser-mode tests, so this is the one to fix first.
  - **MODERATE — `@sveltejs/kit <=2.70.1`:** prototype pollution in the remote-function form file-input deletion path ([GHSA-866w-xmhq-wj7x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-866w-xmhq-wj7x)), plus a Node crash on large remote-form payloads ([GHSA-wqjv-9729-c5q2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wqjv-9729-c5q2)). We don't use remote functions today, but this is shipped framework code.
  - **HIGH — `postcss <=8.5.17`:** path traversal via `sourceMappingURL` auto-loading discloses arbitrary `.map` files ([GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849)).
  - **HIGH — `js-yaml 4.0.0–4.2.0`:** merge-key chains force quadratic CPU ([GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m)). Build-time only.
  - **HIGH — `brace-expansion <=5.0.7`:** exponential-time expansion and unbounded expansion length ([GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp), [GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg)). Transitive via glob/eslint; build-time only.

### Correctness / infrastructure

- **Stack-dependent suites are still outside the gate.** The build gate (`vercel.json` → `npm run verify`) covers `check`, `check:deno`, `lint`, and the node-side Vitest project; the `client` browser project runs advisory-only in GitHub Actions. `test:e2e` and `test:integration` need a live Supabase stack and run nowhere automatically. Decide whether they earn a scheduled job — that is also the natural home for the service-drift check below.
- **The RLS integration suite un-skips on an env var, and would then break the gate.** `family-category-visibility.spec.ts` sits in the `server` Vitest project, so `npm run verify` collects it every run; it skips only because `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is unset. Add that key to Vercel's build environment (an easy thing to do for an unrelated reason) and the 8 tests flip from skipped to failing with `TypeError: fetch failed` — no Postgres is reachable from a build container — and every deploy is blocked with a misleading error. Same trap locally for anyone who exports the key. Options: move the suite out of the `server` project into its own Vitest project that `verify` doesn't run, or make the skip condition an explicit opt-in flag (`RUN_RLS_TESTS=1`) rather than the incidental presence of a credential. Documented for now in [local-dev.md](local-dev.md#testing).
- **`receipts.family_id` is nullable, but a Receipt must always belong to a Family.** The intended invariant is that a Receipt cannot exist without a `family_id`; the schema does not enforce it. The column is declared `"family_id" "uuid"` with no `NOT NULL` (baseline `:607`, confirmed live as `is_nullable = YES`), and `receipts_family_id_fkey` is **`ON DELETE SET NULL`** (`:946`) — so deleting a Family silently orphans its Receipts rather than being prevented or cascading. All four receipts RLS policies then carry an explicit `family_id IS NULL → fall back to owner (user_id)` branch (`:1021` insert, `:1049` delete, `:1061` update, `:1073` select), so an orphan reverts to owner-private and disappears for every other family member. **`expense_categories` has no such fallback** — its policy joins `receipts r → family_members fm ON fm.family_id = r.family_id` (`:1151`), so an orphaned Receipt's category row becomes invisible and unmanageable to _everyone, including its owner_. That inconsistency is the sharpest symptom. The nullability also propagates into application types (`InsertedReceiptRow` in `ReceiptService.ts:41`, and the receipts entry in `src/lib/tests/builders/testDatabase.ts`) and into the `apply_vendor_rule_after_insert` trigger, which skips rows whose `family_id` is null. Fixing it: **decide family-deletion semantics first** — `RESTRICT` (block deleting a Family that still owns Receipts) is safer than `CASCADE` (deleting a Family destroys its Receipts and their stored files). Then backfill any existing NULLs, `SET NOT NULL`, replace the FK action, drop the `IS NULL` branches from the four policies, and simplify the types. One case needs a deliberate answer: `set_receipt_family_id` (`:387`) fills the column from `ensure_default_family()`, which **can return null** — under `NOT NULL` that insert would fail loudly instead of silently producing an orphan, which is probably correct but is a behaviour change for any path where the user has no default family.
- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (originally `003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, carried into the baseline). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path — they survive only if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback. Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert in a new migration and confirm the remote function matches.
- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That is the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by reading the year in a **`+page.ts` `load`** (`data.year`) with the arrows using **`goto`** — `load` re-runs with the right URL on every navigation. (Client-side derivation did NOT hold up: both `$app/stores` `$page` and the `$app/state` reactive `page` went stale on Back.) Apply the same `load`-based pattern here, and audit any other `$derived(… $page.url …)` site. Latent — not yet reproduced for expenses.
- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle was specced but never built. **Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.**
- **Local Supabase service versions drift silently from production.** `supabase/.temp/*-version` records the remote project's service versions **as of the last `supabase link`** and `supabase start` runs exactly those images, so local mirrors whatever prod looked like at link time. Supabase keeps upgrading the hosted project; local never moves. The pins sat at 2025-11-27 for eight months, leaving local on `gotrue v2.183.0` / `storage-api v1.31.1` against prod's `v2.193.1` / `v1.67.15` — i.e. we develop and test auth and storage, the two services `receipts` signed-URL security rests on, against versions prod stopped running long ago. `supabase start` printed the warning on every single start; nobody reads a warning in a 15-line startup log. Fixed for now by re-linking (see [Local development](local-dev.md)), but it will re-open. **Detection is scriptable:** read the four `.temp/*-version` files and diff against the `remote` field of `supabase services --output json`. Do _not_ diff against that command's `local` field — that reports the CLI's bundled defaults, not what is actually running, and yields permanent false positives. Best home is a scheduled job once CI exists; a local pre-`db:up` check would be per-developer and easy to ignore.
- **`adapter-auto` leaves the deploy target implicit.** `svelte.config.js` still uses the scaffold default, which infers the adapter from build-time env vars — on Vercel that resolves to `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel`. It works, and nothing is broken. But the choice of Node vs Edge runtime, region, and per-route function config is currently whatever the auto-detect picks, which matters for the long-running Mistral OCR calls. Pin `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel` explicitly when convenient and set the runtime deliberately. Low priority.
- **`allowScripts` is stale for `esbuild` — install scripts are being blocked.** `npm ci` warns: `esbuild@0.28.1 (postinstall: node install.js)` is not covered by the `allowScripts` map in `package.json`, which still lists only `esbuild@0.27.7`. Two esbuild copies exist in the lockfile — `0.27.7` at the root (used by Vite/Vitest, approved) and `0.28.1` nested under `tsx` (not approved). The current CI job is unaffected because `npm run verify` never invokes `tsx`, but the `seed:demo` scripts do. Either approve `esbuild@0.28.1` or confirm the nested copy works without its postinstall.
- **Watch for storage-policy drift.** `supabase db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are hand-maintained at the end of `20260726120000_baseline.sql`. A future storage change written only as a migration will be lost the next time the baseline is regenerated; one made only in the dashboard will never reach a new environment. Consider a check that diffs live storage policies against the baseline.
- **Emailed receipts are never resized — the two capture paths store different things.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes straight to storage (`supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts:137`) with no size check and no resize, so a receipt forwarded by email is stored at whatever size the sender's mail client produced, while the same receipt uploaded in the browser becomes a 2400px JPEG. Deliberate for now — it is a Deno edge function with no Canvas, so matching it means a WASM image library plus a second copy of the resize rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/` kept in lock-step by hand (the burden CLAUDE.md already flags for the date-correction code), and CPU time inside a webhook that must answer quickly. Recorded as an accepted asymmetry in [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) and the ["Every uploaded image becomes JPEG" invariant](domain-model.md). Revisit if storage cost or emailed-receipt volume grows.
- **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
- **`ReceiptService` ships debug logging to production.** Three `console.log`s on the receipts-page load path (`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:84`, `:91`, `:101`) print the user id, the **full `family_members` rows for that user**, and the fetched receipt payload to the browser console on every visit. The middle one is a query run purely to log its result — it is labelled "for debugging" and nothing consumes it. A fourth logs every created receipt in `insertReceiptOrCleanupUpload` (`:347`); it is the only remaining reader of `family_id` on `InsertedReceiptRow`, so deleting it may let that type collapse back to `ReceiptRow`. Delete the logs and the debug query.
- **Receipts page fetches every family expense just to colour one column.** `loadCategories` (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:254`) calls `ExpenseService.getExpenses` — a full paged pass over `receipts` with an embed — solely to build `categoryMap` for the edit modal. Adding the Category column (see [Classify on the Receipts page](plans/2026-08-03-classify-on-receipts-page-design.md)) puts that second full-table read on the render path, on a page that has already loaded every receipt once. It should read `expense_categories` for the receipts already in hand instead.
- **Garbled OCR merchant names create junk and orphaned vendor rules.** `ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` (`:321`) only lowercases and strips punctuation, so store numbers survive: `"STARBUCKS #1234"` becomes the pattern `starbucks 1234`, which will never match another receipt. The Receipts Category column makes this worse by design — it is the fast path, so people will categorize from the list _before_ opening the modal to clean up the merchant name, and fixing the name afterwards orphans the rule that was just created against the old one. Needs a normalization rule that drops trailing store/terminal numbers, and pairs with the vendor-rule management UI under Features (today these rules are invisible and unremovable).
- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for the nothing-found-anywhere row, but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case. The tests assert the real `422`; the PRD table is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the table or leave the note.

## Refactoring

Every catalogued refactoring (**RF-01→13**, plus code-review follow-ups
**RV-01→11**) has landed — see [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md) for the
per-item Landed notes. The only other outstanding entries are the two deferred
value-object questions, **RF-D1** (`Money`) and **RF-D2** (typed date) — both a
recorded _keep-primitives_ decision, not scheduled work. New refactoring ideas start
here as one-liners and get promoted to an `RF-NN` entry only when work begins.

- **Delete the dead `#{#...}` spec tags.** `src/` carries **649** traceability tags
  (**179** distinct, across **64** files) of the form `#{#exp2a}`, `#{#vca5a}`,
  `#{#rmc2a}` — plus prose headers naming files like
  `specs/specifications/expense-categorization.md`. **That directory does not exist**:
  it was deleted deliberately in `92e9ae1` ("Kill off specs", 2026-07-06), and
  `CLAUDE.md` does not list the tags as a convention. Every one is now a reference to
  nothing, and they cost real time — tracing `#{#vca2a}` to its (non-existent) source
  took several minutes during the Receipts categorization work. They also **propagate**:
  the convention is invisible-but-contagious, so anyone editing tagged code copies the
  tags into new code, as happened in that change. Worse, deleting tagged code can strand
  a tag on its last remaining reference — `#{#vca2a}` briefly survived only on a comment
  explaining that the behaviour it named no longer happened there. A sweep is
  mechanical (regex-removable) but touches 64 files, so it wants its own commit and its
  own review, and should land alongside a `CLAUDE.md` note so the convention is not
  reintroduced. Decide first whether any tag is still load-bearing — grep suggests not,
  since nothing resolves them.

## Open questions

- **Combining receipts for one expense.** How to handle when two receipts should be combined into one expense to match — e.g. two medications picked up at the same time.
- **WealthSimple refund handling.** WealthSimple records several rows when a refund is issued. Example:

  ```csv
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-24","Refund initiated","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","33.9","CAD"
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"

1	# Classify / Reclassify on the Receipts Page — Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-03

10	You can classify an expense on the Expenses page. On the Receipts page you can
11	only do it by opening a receipt's edit modal — where the dropdown is clipped out
12	of view, which is the logged bug _"Category dropdown clipped"_. So in practice
13	the Receipts page cannot classify anything.
14	
15	Fixing that turned out to be two changes, not one. The visible half is a Category
16	column on the receipts table plus a dropdown that stops being clipped. The
17	invisible half is larger and more valuable: **vendor rules move from the client to
18	the database**, so a receipt is categorized when it is created rather than when
19	someone happens to visit the right page.
20	
21	## What exists today
22	
23	The Expenses page has the full feature — a `category` column marked
24	`interactive: true` so clicking it does not open the receipt modal
25	(`src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte:1236`, `DataTable.svelte:179`), rendering
26	`CategoryDropdown` with search, keyboard navigation, inline category creation and
27	a vendor-rule panel. `handleCategorySelect` (`:282`) persists immediately,
28	auto-creates a vendor rule, applies it to other visible rows, toasts, and fans out
29	to a multi-row selection via `applyCategoryToSelection` (`:208`).

31	The Receipts page has none of it. Its table is Image / Date / Merchant / Amount /
32	Actions (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:908`) — no Category column, so you
33	cannot see which receipts are uncategorized, let alone change one. The only path
34	is the edit modal, and `ReceiptEditModal` wraps its body in `overflow-y-auto p-6`
35	(`:234`), which is exactly the clipping trap CLAUDE.md documents: a container
36	whose overflow is non-visible in one axis clips absolutely-positioned children in
37	_both_.

39	`handleCategoryChange` on the receipts page (`:263`) has also drifted from its
40	Expenses twin — it assigns and creates a rule, but never applies the rule to other
41	rows and shows no feedback at all.
42	
43	### The domain-model tension, and why we are crossing it
44	
45	[The domain model](../domain-model.md) says: _"Talk about Expenses when reporting
46	or categorizing; talk about Receipts when capturing."_ This design puts
47	categorizing on the capture surface.
48	
49	That line was already crossed by the edit modal (`#{#rmc2a}`), so the column is a

# Classify / Reclassify on the Receipts Page — Design

**Date:** 2026-08-03
**Status:** ✅ Built (pending release) — Category column on Receipts, `CategoryDropdown`
repositioned with `@floating-ui/dom`, vendor rules applied by an AFTER INSERT trigger,
`autoAssignCategoryBestEffort` deleted, sweep added to the Receipts page. The
[deferred RPC move](#deferred-finish-the-migration-and-delete-the-typescript-normalizer)
is still deferred, and the [split-receipt question](#out-of-scope) is still open.

You can classify an expense on the Expenses page. On the Receipts page you can
only do it by opening a receipt's edit modal — where the dropdown is clipped out
of view, which is the logged bug _"Category dropdown clipped"_. So in practice
the Receipts page cannot classify anything.

Fixing that turned out to be two changes, not one. The visible half is a Category
column on the receipts table plus a dropdown that stops being clipped. The
invisible half is larger and more valuable: **vendor rules move from the client to
the database**, so a receipt is categorized when it is created rather than when
someone happens to visit the right page.

## What exists today

The Expenses page has the full feature — a `category` column marked
`interactive: true` so clicking it does not open the receipt modal
(`src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte:1236`, `DataTable.svelte:179`), rendering
`CategoryDropdown` with search, keyboard navigation, inline category creation and
a vendor-rule panel. `handleCategorySelect` (`:282`) persists immediately,
auto-creates a vendor rule, applies it to other visible rows, toasts, and fans out
to a multi-row selection via `applyCategoryToSelection` (`:208`).

The Receipts page has none of it. Its table is Image / Date / Merchant / Amount /
Actions (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:908`) — no Category column, so you
cannot see which receipts are uncategorized, let alone change one. The only path
is the edit modal, and `ReceiptEditModal` wraps its body in `overflow-y-auto p-6`
(`:234`), which is exactly the clipping trap CLAUDE.md documents: a container
whose overflow is non-visible in one axis clips absolutely-positioned children in
_both_.

`handleCategoryChange` on the receipts page (`:263`) has also drifted from its
Expenses twin — it assigns and creates a rule, but never applies the rule to other
rows and shows no feedback at all.

### The domain-model tension, and why we are crossing it

[The domain model](../domain-model.md) says: _"Talk about Expenses when reporting
or categorizing; talk about Receipts when capturing."_ This design puts
categorizing on the capture surface.

That line was already crossed by the edit modal (`#{#rmc2a}`), so the column is a
consistency fix rather than a new boundary violation. The workflow argument is the
real one: you upload a batch of receipts, you are looking at them, and the app
sends you to a different page to say what they are. The glossary entry should be
amended when this lands rather than left contradicting the UI.

## Changes

### 1. Category column on the receipts table

Between Amount and Actions, `interactive: true`, rendering the existing
`CategoryDropdown` — the same arrangement as Expenses.

Behaviour is **identical to the Expenses column**, via one extracted
implementation rather than a third copy of the same logic:

- persists immediately on pick, no Save;
- auto-creates a vendor rule for that merchant when none exists;
- applies that new rule to other visible uncategorized rows;
- toasts the count;
- picking a category on a row that is part of a multi-row selection sets the
  whole selection.

Two supporting edits. `applyRuleToVisibleExpenses` (`ExpenseService.ts:414`)
currently takes `Expense[]`, but the receipts page holds `ReceiptRow[]` plus a
separate `categoryMap`; it only reads `receipt_id`, `merchant_name` and
`category_id`, so its parameter type widens to those three fields. And the
receipts page already owns `receiptSelection`, so the fan-out costs almost
nothing.

**No sort on the column and no Uncategorized filter.** The Receipts FilterPanel
already carries six controls and the uncategorized queue belongs on Expenses.

### 2. The dropdown stops being clipped

`@floating-ui/dom` is promoted to a direct dependency. It is already resolved in
the lockfile as a dependency of `flowbite-svelte@1.33.1` (which we use for
`Datepicker`), so this adds no new supply-chain surface and `min-release-age` is
not a factor.

intact — this is a positioning change to one `<div>`.

One fix closes three bugs:

| Where                                                           | Clipping container                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Receipt edit modal — the logged bug                             | `ReceiptEditModal.svelte:234`, `overflow-y-auto p-6`            |
| The new Receipts column, on phones                              | `DataTable.svelte:108`, `overflow-x-auto … sm:overflow-visible` |
| The Expenses column, on phones — **broken in production today** | same line                                                       |

Rebuilding `CategoryDropdown` on flowbite-svelte's own `Dropdown` was considered
and rejected: it wraps the same library but would restructure a component
carrying search, keyboard nav, inline creation and the vendor-rule panel, for the
same outcome.

### 5. What does not change

The edit modal keeps its deferred Save/Cancel contract for category

_inside a Save/Cancel modal everything defers; direct manipulation in the table is

## Testing

Trigger coverage goes in the integration suite, alongside

precedent: it drives `vendor_category_rules` and `expense_categories` against a
