**Date:** 2026-08-03
**Status:** 📋 Designed, not built. Decisions below were settled in a grilling session
on 2026-08-03; two open items are marked inline as
[assumptions](#assumptions-made-not-decided).

A Receipt records merchant, amount and date, and nothing else a person can say in
their own words. Everything else the app knows is either extracted from the image
or inferred. So there is nowhere to write down _"Sam's birthday gift"_,
_"reimbursable — client dinner"_, or _"warranty runs to 2028"_ — the reasons a
purchase actually mattered.

This adds one free-text field to the Receipt, editable in the receipt edit modal,
with a truncated preview on the Receipts and Expenses lists.

It is a small feature that lands on top of a real bug. Adding a column to
`receipts` means touching **five hand-maintained field lists**, none of which the
compiler checks — and one of the five is a synthetic `ReceiptRow` on the Expenses
page that is **already silently destroying data in production**. That fix is in
scope, because notes walk straight into it.

## What exists today

`receipts` has no note-like column (`supabase/migrations/20260726120000_baseline.sql:595`)
and nothing in `Receipt.ts` is close. `ReceiptEditModal` (shared by the Receipts,
Expenses and Reconciliation pages) edits nine fields; both list pages render an
explicit `DataTable` `columns` array (`receipts/+page.svelte:908`,
`expenses/+page.svelte:1220`).

### The five field lists

| # | Location | Silent failure if `notes` is omitted |
| - | -------- | ------------------------------------ |
| 1 | `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (`ReceiptService.ts:118`) | `update()` strips the field. No error, no save. |
| 2 | patch literal, Receipts page (`+page.svelte:218`) | Note never saves from Receipts |
| 3 | patch literal, Reconciliation page (`+page.svelte:384`) | Note never saves from Reconciliation |
| 4 | patch literal, Expenses page (`+page.svelte:555`) | Note never saves from Expenses |
| 5 | `isDirty` in the modal (`ReceiptEditModal.svelte:68`) | Closing with an unsaved note gives **no warning** — the note is discarded |

All five are inferred object literals or a string `Set`, so omitting a field
type-checks cleanly. They have already drifted: the Receipts patch carries
`suspicious_date` (`:228`) and the Reconciliation patch does not (`:392`).

### The bug this feature would have inherited

`openReceiptEditModal` on the Expenses page (`expenses/+page.svelte:524`) builds a
**synthetic `ReceiptRow`** from the `Expense` projection, hard-coding every field
`Expense` does not carry:

```js
tax: null,
credit_card_name: null,
credit_card_last_4: null,
matched_transaction_id: null,   // Expense DOES carry this — it is discarded anyway
suspicious_date: false,
```

`handleReceiptSave` (`:550`) then writes all of them back (`:559`–`:566`).

**Open any receipt from the Expenses page, change nothing, press Save — and you
erase its tax amount, card name, last-4 digits, and its reconciliation match.** A
receipt matched to a TD transaction becomes unmatched. This is live today and
predates this feature.

`notes` would have joined that list, and worse: the whole point of §4 below is to
show the note on the Expenses list, so people will click that row _because they
saw the note_, and destroy it.

Reconciliation gets this right already — `openReceiptEditModal` there
(`reconciliation/+page.svelte:350`) fetches the real row with `select('*')`.

## Decisions

Each was put as a question and answered; the reasoning is kept because the
alternatives are not obviously wrong.

**A note is human-authored, and the app may only seed it at capture time.** OCR or
scan-time extraction may write a note _before_ any person can see the receipt.
From the moment a receipt is visible in the app, the note is the family's. There
is no `source` column and no author attribution, because the temporal ordering
makes conflict impossible: a machine write after a human has seen the receipt is
a bug, not a case to model.

**Splits copy the note.** `buildSplitReceiptInsert` (`ReceiptService.ts:598`) is an
explicit whitelist, so this had to be chosen rather than defaulted. A note is
identity ("Sam's birthday"), and the domain model already frames a Split Receipt
as a full Receipt inheriting the original's identity — merchant, card, currency
and image all carry over. Copying is also the recoverable error: the person opens
the split and deletes two sentences. Blanking is unrecoverable, because nothing
tells them a note was ever there.

**1024 characters, a `<textarea>`, newlines allowed.** Notes will usually be
short, but the ceiling costs nothing and the one time someone needs to write out a
warranty claim the field should not fight them. A single-line `<input>` for
something people will occasionally paste a paragraph into is miserable to edit.

**No `maxlength`.** Type and paste freely; a counter appears near the limit and
Save is blocked past it with an inline message. `maxlength` **silently truncates a
paste** — the person sees text, saves, and never learns the last sentence is gone.
That is the one failure here you cannot detect afterwards. Blocking Save puts the
choice of what to cut where it belongs.

**Preview lives under the merchant name, not in its own column.** `DataTable`'s
container is `overflow-x-auto … sm:overflow-visible` (`:108`) — deliberately
visible on desktop so category dropdowns are not clipped — so a table that outgrows
its width on desktop **overflows with no scrollbar**, and there is no responsive
column hiding. Expenses is already at five columns plus a checkbox. A second line
in the merchant cell costs nothing on the ~90% of rows with no note, and reads the
way you would say it aloud: "Costco, Sam's birthday gift".

**Modal only — no note field on manual create.** The counter-argument is real: a
Manual Receipt has no image, so merchant/amount/date is everything the app knows
and the note would be the only place detail can live. It lost to duplication —
the validation story above would have to exist on a second surface, and the table
at the top of this document is what happens in this codebase when one thing is
maintained in two places. Create, then click the row you just created. If manual
entry turns out to be the dominant note-taking case, adding it later is cheap
_because_ the validation will already be factored out.

## Changes

### 1. Migration

```sql
ALTER TABLE public.receipts ADD COLUMN notes text;
ALTER TABLE public.receipts ADD CONSTRAINT receipts_notes_length
  CHECK (notes IS NULL OR char_length(notes) <= 1024);
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.receipts.notes IS
  'Free-text note about the purchase. Human-authored; the app may only write it at
   capture time, before anyone can see the receipt. See docs/domain-model.md.';
```

Nullable, no default. `NULL` means "no note" — the modal normalizes a
whitespace-only field back to `NULL` on save so that empty string and null do not
become two spellings of nothing.

The `CHECK` is the real limit. Client validation is UX; three write paths do not
go through the modal (email ingestion in `supabase/functions/`,
`ExpenseImportService`, and the capture-time seeding described above) and any of
them could grow a note-writing branch.

Verify with `npm run db:reset` before pushing.

No index. Notes are not searched (see [Deferred](#deferred)) and are read only as
part of a row already being fetched.

### 2. Model and the five field lists

`ReceiptRow` and `ReceiptInsert` gain `notes: string | null` / `notes?: string | null`;
`Receipt` gains the private field, constructor assignment, `toRow()` entry and
getter, following `original_filename` exactly.

`#EDITABLE_FIELDS` gains `'notes'`.

**The three page-level patch literals collapse into one `buildReceiptPatch(row)`**
used by all three pages. Five hand-maintained lists become three, and the next
field added to `receipts` cannot be half-wired. The `suspicious_date` drift
between the Receipts and Reconciliation patches is flattened deliberately:
`ReceiptService.update` forces `suspicious_date = false` whenever
`transaction_date` is present (`:151`), and both patches always send
`transaction_date`, so the two pages already behave identically and the difference
is vestigial. _(Assumption — see below.)_

`isDirty` in the modal gains `editedReceipt.notes !== receipt.notes`. Miss this
and closing a modal with an unsaved note discards it with no prompt.

### 3. The field in the modal

A `<textarea>` in the form column of `ReceiptEditModal`, below Category, labelled
**Note (optional)** to match the existing "(optional)" convention on the other
fields. Three or four rows.

Validation, reusing the modal's existing machinery — an `error` state rendered at
the top of the body (`:236`) and the save-time validation precedent in
`hasMinimumData` (`:128`):

- a character counter appears from ~900 characters and turns red past 1024;
- past 1024, Save is disabled with an inline message naming the overage;
- no `maxlength` attribute.

The note does **not** count toward the minimum-data rule — a receipt with only a
note and no merchant, amount or date is still invalid. That rule is about whether
the app has enough to identify a purchase, and a note does not identify one.

One detail needing no special handling: JS `.length` counts UTF-16 units while
Postgres `char_length` counts characters, so an emoji is 2 to the browser and 1 to
the database. That skews conservative — the client can never let through something
the `CHECK` rejects.

### 4. Preview on both list pages

A second line inside the existing merchant cell, rendered only when a note is
present:

```
Costco
Sam's birthday gift — ask Jen about the receipt
```

Smaller, grey, single line, CSS `truncate` for the ellipsis, newlines collapsed to
spaces, with the full text in a `title` attribute. This is precisely the treatment
`original_filename` already gets (`ReceiptEditModal.svelte:323`).

`title` is a bonus, not the affordance — it does not work on touch or keyboard.
The real "read the rest" gesture is clicking the row, which already opens the
modal.

Consequence worth naming: "a few characters" is not a fixed budget here, it is
however much fits the column at the current window width. A fixed budget (first 60
characters, then `…`, regardless of width) would need JS truncation instead. CSS
was chosen; say so if the variability is wrong.

The Receipts page gets `notes` for free — `ReceiptService.list` selects `*`
(`:97`). `ExpenseService.getExpenses` uses an explicit select list, so `Expense`
gains `notes: string | null` and the select gains the column. Note that on
`Expense` this is a **display projection only** — the modal gets its data from the
fetch in §5, not from the row.

### 5. The Expenses page stops synthesizing a receipt

`ReceiptService` gains `getById(id)` — a `select('*').eq('id', id).single()`, which
is what the Reconciliation page already does inline (`:354`) and what
`fetchOriginalForSplit` (`:565`) does privately. Both should be moved onto it.

`openReceiptEditModal` on the Expenses page awaits `getById` and passes the real
row to the modal, replacing the synthetic literal at `:526`–`:542`. One extra
round-trip on row click, on a click that already opens a modal and fetches a signed
image URL.

This removes the whole class of defect rather than the instance: every field added
to `receipts` from now on inherits the bug otherwise, `notes` being the next one.

Chosen over adding `notes` to the `Expense` projection and threading it into the
synthetic row, which would have made notes safe while tax, card details and the
reconciliation match kept being erased — and widened the pattern that caused it.

### 6. Splits

`buildSplitReceiptInsert` gains `notes: original.notes`.

While in there: `original_filename` is **not** in that whitelist, so a split
silently loses its filename today. Same class, one line. Out of scope here but
worth a look while the file is open.

## Testing

Node-project (gated) unit coverage:

- `buildReceiptPatch` includes `notes` — the test that would have caught four of
  the five field lists.
- `ReceiptService.update` passes `notes` through `#EDITABLE_FIELDS` and strips a
  bogus sibling.
- `splitReceipt` copies the note to the split.
- Whitespace-only note normalizes to `NULL`.
- Length validation at 1023 / 1024 / 1025 characters.

Modal component tests (`client` project, advisory only per
[ADR-0005](../adr/0005-quality-gate-in-the-vercel-build-not-github-actions.md)):

- `isDirty` fires on a note edit, so the discard prompt appears.
- Save is blocked past 1024 with the message shown.
- Preview truncates and collapses newlines.

The `CHECK` constraint itself is only reachable with a live stack, so it belongs in
`npm run test:integration` — which gates nothing. Same accepted position as the
vendor-rule trigger, and for the same reason.

**The regression test that matters most is the §5 one:** open a receipt with a tax
amount and a matched transaction from the Expenses page, save without editing,
assert both survive. That is the bug, and it is invisible to every existing test.

## Risks

**The five lists are the whole risk.** Every failure mode here is silent — no
error, no type error, just a field that does not persist or a warning that does not
appear. §2 exists to shrink the surface, but `#EDITABLE_FIELDS` and `isDirty`
remain hand-maintained and cannot be checked by the compiler.

**Notes are shared and last-write-wins.** `Members can update family receipts`
(`baseline.sql:1061`) lets any active family member edit any family receipt, and
nothing records who wrote a note or when. Two people editing the same note
concurrently means one loses their text with no indication. Acceptable at family
scale, and consistent with how every other receipt field already behaves — but it
is a property of the design, not an oversight.

**Split notes diverge.** Peers hold independent copies; editing one leaves the
others stale, and nothing links or flags them. This follows from "a split is a
full Receipt" and is the accepted cost of the copy decision.

## Assumptions made, not decided

Two branches the design settled without an explicit ruling. Both are cheap to
reverse; flagged so neither is mistaken for a decision.

1. **Exports are untouched in this change.** The session identified the CSV column
   (~2 lines — one header entry, one `escapeCSVField` call in `buildRow`;
   `escapeCSVField` already quotes commas, quotes _and_ newlines, and
   `parseExpenseImportCsv` ignores columns it does not need, so re-import is
   unaffected) and the PDF **per-receipt page** (one line under the existing
   reference header, `PDFExportService.ts:470`/`:506`) as the two worth doing. Both
   are read here as deferred to the backlog. If the CSV column was meant to ship
   with this, it is a two-line addition to §1's scope.
2. **The name is `notes` (column) / "Note" (label and domain term).** Plural is the
   near-universal column convention; the singular reads correctly in the UI and
   glossary because a Receipt has exactly one.
3. **The `suspicious_date` drift between the two patch literals is vestigial.**
   §2 flattens it. If Reconciliation deliberately omits it, `buildReceiptPatch`
   needs a parameter instead — but `update()` (`:151`) makes both paths behave
   identically today, so there is no observable difference to preserve.

## Deferred

- **Note in the CSV export** and **note on the PDF per-receipt page.** Logged in
  the backlog.
- **Searching or filtering by note.** Neither list page has free-text search today
  (Receipts filters on merchant/amount/needs-review/duplicates; Expenses on
  date/category/uncategorized), so this is a new capability rather than an
  extension, and "just a bit of text" is the stated bar. Logged as an open
  question.
- **Notes on the manual-create form.** See the decision above.
- **Attribution and history** — who wrote a note, when, and what it said before.
  Ruled out in the first question; would mean a `receipt_notes` table rather than a
  column.

## Sequencing

1. Migration (`notes` + `CHECK`), verified with `npm run db:reset`.
2. `ReceiptRow` / `ReceiptInsert` / `Receipt`, and `#EDITABLE_FIELDS`.
3. Extract `buildReceiptPatch`, adopt it on all three pages. Independently
   shippable — it is a pure refactor that fixes the existing `suspicious_date`
   drift before any note code depends on it.
4. `ReceiptService.getById`; Expenses page stops synthesizing. **Also independently
   shippable, and it fixes a live data-loss bug** — worth landing on its own,
   ahead of the rest, with the regression test from Testing above.
5. Textarea + counter + validation in the modal; `isDirty`.
6. `notes` on the `Expense` projection and select; preview line on both list pages.
7. `notes: original.notes` in `buildSplitReceiptInsert`.
8. Amend the [domain model](../domain-model.md) — the **Note** entry and its
   authority invariant.

Version number is assigned by hand at commit time.

to `receipts` from now on inherits the bug otherwise, `notes` being the next one.

Chosen over adding `notes` to the `Expense` projection and threading it into the
synthetic row, which would have made notes safe while tax, card details and the
reconciliation match kept being erased — and widened the pattern that caused it.

### 6. Splits

`buildSplitReceiptInsert` gains `notes: original.notes`.

While in there: `original_filename` is **not** in that whitelist, so a split
silently loses its filename today. Same class, one line. Out of scope here but
worth a look while the file is open.

## Testing

Node-project (gated) unit coverage:

- `buildReceiptPatch` includes `notes` — the test that would have caught four of
  the five field lists.
- `ReceiptService.update` passes `notes` through `#EDITABLE_FIELDS` and strips a
  bogus sibling.
- `splitReceipt` copies the note to the split.
- Whitespace-only note normalizes to `NULL`.
- Length validation at 1023 / 1024 / 1025 characters.

Modal component tests (`client` project, advisory only per
[ADR-0005](../adr/0005-quality-gate-in-the-vercel-build-not-github-actions.md)):

- `isDirty` fires on a note edit, so the discard prompt appears.
- Save is blocked past 1024 with the message shown.
- Preview truncates and collapses newlines.

The `CHECK` constraint itself is only reachable with a live stack, so it belongs in
`npm run test:integration` — which gates nothing. Same accepted position as the
vendor-rule trigger, and for the same reason.

**The regression test that matters most is the §5 one:** open a receipt with a tax
amount and a matched transaction from the Expenses page, save without editing,
assert both survive. That is the bug, and it is invisible to every existing test.

## Risks

**The five lists are the whole risk.** Every failure mode here is silent — no
error, no type error, just a field that does not persist or a warning that does not
appear. §2 exists to shrink the surface, but `#EDITABLE_FIELDS` and `isDirty`
remain hand-maintained and cannot be checked by the compiler.

**Notes are shared and last-write-wins.** `Members can update family receipts`
(`baseline.sql:1061`) lets any active family member edit any family receipt, and
nothing records who wrote a note or when. Two people editing the same note
concurrently means one loses their text with no indication. Acceptable at family
scale, and consistent with how every other receipt field already behaves — but it
is a property of the design, not an oversight.

**Split notes diverge.** Peers hold independent copies; editing one leaves the
others stale, and nothing links or flags them. This follows from "a split is a
full Receipt" and is the accepted cost of the copy decision.

## Assumptions made, not decided

Two branches the design settled without an explicit ruling. Both are cheap to
reverse; flagged so neither is mistaken for a decision.

1. **Exports are untouched in this change.** The session identified the CSV column
   (~2 lines — one header entry, one `escapeCSVField` call in `buildRow`;
   `escapeCSVField` already quotes commas, quotes _and_ newlines, and
   `parseExpenseImportCsv` ignores columns it does not need, so re-import is
   unaffected) and the PDF **per-receipt page** (one line under the existing
   reference header, `PDFExportService.ts:470`/`:506`) as the two worth doing. Both
   are read here as deferred to the backlog. If the CSV column was meant to ship
   with this, it is a two-line addition to §1's scope.
2. **The name is `notes` (column) / "Note" (label and domain term).** Plural is the
   near-universal column convention; the singular reads correctly in the UI and
   glossary because a Receipt has exactly one.
3. **The `suspicious_date` drift between the two patch literals is vestigial.**
   §2 flattens it. If Reconciliation deliberately omits it, `buildReceiptPatch`
   needs a parameter instead — but `update()` (`:151`) makes both paths behave
   identically today, so there is no observable difference to preserve.

## Deferred

- **Note in the CSV export** and **note on the PDF per-receipt page.** Logged in
  the backlog.
- **Searching or filtering by note.** Neither list page has free-text search today
  (Receipts filters on merchant/amount/needs-review/duplicates; Expenses on
  date/category/uncategorized), so this is a new capability rather than an
  extension, and "just a bit of text" is the stated bar. Logged as an open
  question.
- **Notes on the manual-create form.** See the decision above.
- **Attribution and history** — who wrote a note, when, and what it said before.
  Ruled out in the first question; would mean a `receipt_notes` table rather than a
  column.

## Sequencing

1. Migration (`notes` + `CHECK`), verified with `npm run db:reset`.
2. `ReceiptRow` / `ReceiptInsert` / `Receipt`, and `#EDITABLE_FIELDS`.
3. Extract `buildReceiptPatch`, adopt it on all three pages. Independently
   shippable — it is a pure refactor that fixes the existing `suspicious_date`
   drift before any note code depends on it.
4. `ReceiptService.getById`; Expenses page stops synthesizing. **Also independently
   shippable, and it fixes a live data-loss bug** — worth landing on its own,
   ahead of the rest, with the regression test from Testing above.
5. Textarea + counter + validation in the modal; `isDirty`.
6. `notes` on the `Expense` projection and select; preview line on both list pages.
7. `notes: original.notes` in `buildSplitReceiptInsert`.
8. Amend the [domain model](../domain-model.md) — the **Note** entry and its
   authority invariant.

Version number is assigned by hand at commit time.

# YFL Expense Tracker

Family expense tracking. Family members capture what they spent — mostly by
uploading receipt images, sometimes by typing the details in by hand — and the
app derives their expenses and reconciles them against imported bank activity.

## Language

**Family**:
The data-scoping unit. All Receipts, Transactions, Categories, and vendor rules
belong to a Family, and every access-control policy scopes to it. Each user gets
one solo Family auto-created at signup (`ensure_default_family()`); their
`is_default` Family is the one they operate on. A `families` row (`id`, `name`).
_Avoid_: household, account

**Family Member**:
A person who belongs to a Family — a `family_members` row (`family_id`,
`user_id`, `role`, `status`, `is_default`). `role ∈ {owner, member}` (the creator
is the `owner`; role is not yet used for authorization). `status ∈ {active,
invited, removed}`, but only `active` rows exist until Invitations ship. A member
is identified for display by their primary email (from `auth.users`), which the
client reads only through the `get_family_members()` `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC.
_Avoid_: user, member, participant

**Receipt**:
A record of a single purchase (merchant, amount, date). May originate from an
uploaded image or be entered by hand. Each Receipt maps to exactly one Expense.
_Avoid_: bill, purchase

**Manual Receipt**:
A Receipt a person creates by typing merchant, amount, and date rather than
uploading an image. It has no image and is not run through OCR; the person is
asserting the details — including the date — directly.
_Avoid_: manual entry, hand receipt

**Expense**:
The categorized view of a Receipt used for reporting. Derived one-to-one from a
Receipt — never stored on its own. Talk about Expenses when reporting; talk about
Receipts when capturing.

Categorizing is deliberately available on **both** surfaces, so it does not
distinguish them. A category can be set from the Receipts list, the Receipts edit
modal, or the Expenses list, and vendor rules are applied by the database the
moment a Receipt is created — categorization is a property of the Receipt's
lifecycle, not something that only happens once you reach a reporting screen.
_Avoid_: cost, spend

**Area of Importance**:
The top tier of the spending hierarchy — e.g. Essential, Priorities, Other. A
family-scoped `importance_areas` row with a `sort_order`. Attaches to the
**Grouping**, not to individual categories, so a Grouping has exactly one
Importance.
_Avoid_: priority band, tier

**Grouping**:
The middle tier of the spending hierarchy — e.g. Everyday, Home, Transportation.
A family-scoped `category_groups` row that belongs to one **Area of Importance**
and gathers many Categories. A Category with no Grouping is _Uncategorized_.
_Avoid_: group, bucket, section

**Spending Report**:
The categorized roll-up of a year's Expenses through Category → Grouping → Area
of Importance, shown as a month-by-month table (the `/spending` "Table" view) or
the **Spending Chart**. Replaces the family's hand-built spreadsheet pivot.
_Avoid_: pivot table, summary

**Spending Chart**:
The charted form of the **Spending Report**: stacked bars (one per Grouping,
stacked by month) with drilldown to Categories — the `/spending` "Chart" view.
_Avoid_: graph, dashboard

**Transaction**:
A line of activity imported from a bank or credit-card statement, reconciled
against Receipts. Distinct from a Receipt: it comes from the bank, not the user.
_Avoid_: charge, payment

**Split Receipt**:
A partial-amount Receipt carved off another. A split is a FULL Receipt record
(not a line-item or child), preserving the 1:1 Receipt↔Expense invariant so no
query or reconciliation code needs to change. Peers share a nullable, indexed
`split_group_id` (UUID). Created by an atomic insert-then-update — the new split
is inserted first, the original reduced second; if the update fails the split is
deleted (best-effort rollback). Both the original's and the split's
`matched_transaction_id` are cleared. Each split takes an optional per-split date
override (deferred charges: hotel/AirBnB/installments) and recomputes
`suspicious_date` from its own date. Splits share the original
`receipt_image_path` — no file is duplicated.
_Avoid_: line item, child receipt

**Source File**:
What a person hands the app — a camera photo, a screenshot, a HEIC picked from
Photos, an attachment on a forwarded email. Transient: it is never stored. Only
its name survives, sanitized into `original_filename`, so people recognize the
receipt by the name they gave it. Its size and format are the app's problem to
absorb, not the person's.
_Avoid_: upload, original, the image

**Receipt Image**:
The single JPEG derived from a **Source File** and stored at
`receipt_image_path` — the only image artifact the app keeps for a Receipt. It
is always JPEG: HEIC and PNG are transcoded on the way in. A PDF receipt is
stored unmodified and is therefore **not** a Receipt Image, which is why it has
no zoom. **Split Receipt** peers share one Receipt Image.
_Avoid_: photo, scan, original, attachment

**Potential Duplicate**:
Two or more Receipts that may record the same purchase — a suspicion raised by
the app, never an assertion. Always _potential_: a family can legitimately hold
two Receipts for the same merchant, amount and day. Duplicate-ness is a property
of a **pair** of Receipts, not of one Receipt, and it is derived on demand rather
than recorded. There is currently no way for a person to settle the suspicion.
_Avoid_: duplicate (unqualified), copy, repeat

## Invariants

**Family-scoped migration invariants**:
When categories and vendor rules moved from user- to family-scope, duplicates
were deduped keeping the FIRST-created row per key; the losing rows' receipt
categorizations become uncategorized via `expense_categories`
`ON DELETE SET NULL`. Category names are unique per family, case-insensitive
(`unique_category_per_family` on `(family_id, LOWER(name))`); vendor patterns are
unique per `(family_id, vendor_pattern)`. Every family-scoped RLS policy requires
`family_members.status = 'active'`. These migrations do not roll back cleanly —
fix forward.

**Foreign-currency reconciliation**:
A Receipt's `total_amount` stays in its ORIGINAL currency; `exchange_rate_to_cad`
is stored on the Receipt at save time (fetched once, never during
reconciliation). Reconciliation matches CAD receipts within a $0.01 tolerance but
foreign-currency receipts within 5% — rate approximation, the ~FX fee, and
settlement timing all move the number. Rates come from the Bank of Canada Valet
API (series `FXEURCAD`, `FXUSDCAD`, `FXGBPCAD`).

**Transaction import dedup**:
Count-based so legitimate in-file repeats survive: for each match key it inserts
`max(0, fileCount − dbCount)` rows, which makes re-import idempotent. The match
key is scoped per family + `credit_card_type`. Excluded rows deliberately count
toward the DB total, so re-importing does not resurrect them.

**Suspicious-date authority**:
Only OCR/automated extraction sets `suspicious_date`. Manual create and any manual
date edit always CLEAR it — user intent is authoritative. Saving through the
receipt edit modal is the confirmation action; there is no separate "confirm
date".

**Suspicious-date scope**:
A suspicious date is a statement that the Receipt's date is untrustworthy, so
that date cannot also be used to decide whether the Receipt is in scope. Counting
or filtering flagged Receipts by the date window would hide exactly the ones
whose date is wrong — they have been filed into the wrong window. The flag is
therefore family-global, deliberately, even while the list beneath it is
date-filtered. Contrast **Split Receipt** grouping, where `split_group_id` is a
trustworthy stored fact and can be resolved globally with no such tension.

**Size limits govern the Receipt Image, not the Source File**:
The 5MB image / 10MB PDF limits state what the family agrees to _store_ — they
describe the **Receipt Image**. A **Source File** is bounded only by a 25MB
ceiling, and that ceiling exists solely to stop an enormous file from exhausting
memory during decode; it is not a statement about acceptable receipts. Asking a
person to shrink a photo the app is about to shrink anyway is asking them to do
the code's job. See [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md).

**Zoom never invents pixels**:
In the receipt viewer 100% means fit-to-viewport, not 1:1, so the zoom ceiling is
a property of the individual image rather than a fixed percentage: it stops at
that image's own natural resolution. Two consequences are deliberate. Zoom
disables itself entirely for an image already at or below viewport size — if
there are no more real pixels there is no more zoom, and a greyed-out control
says so honestly. And storage holds three generations of Receipt Image
(full-resolution from before resizing existed, 2000px, and 2400px), each of
which gets a correct ceiling from its own dimensions with no migration.

**Every uploaded image becomes JPEG**:
HEIC and PNG are transcoded during resize; only PDFs pass through untouched. One
stored format means one set of rules for OCR, display, and storage accounting.
Resizing happens in the browser via Canvas, so this holds only for the upload
path — a receipt arriving by email is stored exactly as it was sent, at whatever
size and format the sender's mail client produced.

**Receipt minimum-data rule**:
A Receipt may be saved with empty fields, but at least ONE of merchant / amount /
date must be non-empty.

**Expense categorization precedence**:
Manual category assignments are never overwritten by auto (vendor-rule)
assignments — auto-categorization only touches uncategorized expenses. New
families get 43 default categories.

input.new_string:
- **🔴 Saving a receipt from the Expenses page erases tax, card details and the reconciliation match.** _(Found 2026-08-03 during the Receipt Notes design.)_ `openReceiptEditModal` (`src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte:524`) builds a **synthetic `ReceiptRow`** from the `Expense` projection, hard-coding every field `Expense` does not carry — `tax: null`, `credit_card_name: null`, `credit_card_last_4: null`, `matched_transaction_id: null`, `suspicious_date: false` (`:533`–`:541`). `handleReceiptSave` (`:550`) then writes all of them back (`:559`–`:566`). So opening any receipt from the **Expenses** page, changing nothing and pressing Save destroys its tax amount, card name and last-4 — and **unmatches a reconciled receipt**. `matched_transaction_id` is the sharpest case: `Expense` genuinely carries it (`ExpenseService.ts:31`) and the synthetic row discards it anyway. The Receipts and Reconciliation pages are unaffected — Reconciliation fetches the real row with `select('*')` (`reconciliation/+page.svelte:350`), which is the fix. **This is a class, not an instance:** every column added to `receipts` from now on inherits it, silently. Fix and regression test are step 4 of [Receipt Notes](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md) (`ReceiptService.getById` + stop synthesizing) and ship independently of that feature. No existing test can see this.
- **Receipt with no date is hard to find.** If a receipt has no date it is hard to locate in the receipts view.

Miss the first four and the field silently never persists — no error; miss the fifth and closing a modal discards an unsaved edit with no prompt. Extracting one `buildReceiptPatch(row)` takes five down to three; it is step 3 of [Receipt Notes](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md) and is a pure refactor that ships on its own.
- **`splitReceipt` silently drops `original_filename`.** `buildSplitReceiptInsert` (`ReceiptService.ts:598`) is an explicit whitelist and does not list it, so a Split Receipt loses the name its Source File arrived under while inheriting merchant, card, currency and image. One line. Same class as the field-list item above — noticed 2026-08-03 while deciding whether splits inherit the new Note (they do).

lines: - **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.

- **`ReceiptService` ships debug logging to production.** Three `console.log`s on the receipts-page load path (`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:84`, `:91`, `:101`) print the user id, the **full `family_members` rows for that user**, and the fetched receipt payload to the browser console on every visit. The middle one is a query run purely to log its result — it is labelled "for debugging" and nothing consumes it. A fourth logs every created receipt in `insertReceiptOrCleanupUpload` (`:347`); it is the only remaining reader of `family_id` on `InsertedReceiptRow`, so deleting it may let that type collapse back to `ReceiptRow`. Delete the logs and the debug query.

- **Receipts page fetches every family expense just to colour one column.** `loadCategories` (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:254`) calls `ExpenseService.getExpenses` — a full paged pass over `receipts` with an embed — solely to build `categoryMap` for the edit modal. Adding the Category column (see [Classify on the Receipts page](plans/2026-08-03-classify-on-receipts-page-design.md)) puts that second full-table read on the render path, on a page that has already loaded every receipt once. It should read `expense_categories` for the receipts already in hand instead.

1	# Receipt Notes — Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-03
4	**Status:** 📋 Designed, not built. Decisions below were settled in a grilling session
5	on 2026-08-03; two open items are marked inline as
6	[assumptions](#assumptions-made-not-decided).
7	
8	A Receipt records merchant, amount and date, and nothing else a person can say in
9	their own words. Everything else the app knows is either extracted from the image
10	or inferred. So there is nowhere to write down _"Sam's birthday gift"_,
11	_"reimbursable — client dinner"_, or _"warranty runs to 2028"_ — the reasons a
12	purchase actually mattered.
13	
14	This adds one free-text field to the Receipt, editable in the receipt edit modal,
15	with a truncated preview on the Receipts and Expenses lists.
16	
17	It is a small feature that lands on top of a real bug. Adding a column to
18	`receipts` means touching **five hand-maintained field lists**, none of which the
19	compiler checks — and one of the five is a synthetic `ReceiptRow` on the Expenses
20	page that is **already silently destroying data in production**. That fix is in
21	scope, because notes walk straight into it.
22	
23	## What exists today
24	
25	`receipts` has no note-like column (`supabase/migrations/20260726120000_baseline.sql:595`)
26	and nothing in `Receipt.ts` is close. `ReceiptEditModal` (shared by the Receipts,
27	Expenses and Reconciliation pages) edits nine fields; both list pages render an
28	explicit `DataTable` `columns` array (`receipts/+page.svelte:908`,
29	`expenses/+page.svelte:1220`).
30	
31	### The five field lists
32	
33	| #   | Location                                                    | Silent failure if `notes` is omitted                                      |
34	| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
35	| 1   | `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (`ReceiptService.ts:118`) | `update()` strips the field. No error, no save.                           |
36	| 2   | patch literal, Receipts page (`+page.svelte:218`)           | Note never saves from Receipts                                            |
37	| 3   | patch literal, Reconciliation page (`+page.svelte:384`)     | Note never saves from Reconciliation                                      |
38	| 4   | patch literal, Expenses page (`+page.svelte:555`)           | Note never saves from Expenses                                            |
39	| 5   | `isDirty` in the modal (`ReceiptEditModal.svelte:68`)       | Closing with an unsaved note gives **no warning** — the note is discarded |
40	
41	All five are inferred object literals or a string `Set`, so omitting a field
42	type-checks cleanly. They have already drifted: the Receipts patch carries
43	`suspicious_date` (`:228`) and the Reconciliation patch does not (`:392`).
44	
45	### The bug this feature would have inherited
46	
47	`openReceiptEditModal` on the Expenses page (`expenses/+page.svelte:524`) builds a
48	**synthetic `ReceiptRow`** from the `Expense` projection, hard-coding every field
49	`Expense` does not carry:
50	
51	```js
52	tax: null,
53	credit_card_name: null,
54	credit_card_last_4: null,
55	matched_transaction_id: null,   // Expense DOES carry this — it is discarded anyway
56	suspicious_date: false,
57	```
58	
59	`handleReceiptSave` (`:550`) then writes all of them back (`:559`–`:566`).
60	
61	**Open any receipt from the Expenses page, change nothing, press Save — and you
62	erase its tax amount, card name, last-4 digits, and its reconciliation match.** A
63	receipt matched to a TD transaction becomes unmatched. This is live today and
64	predates this feature.
65	
66	`notes` would have joined that list, and worse: the whole point of §4 below is to
67	show the note on the Expenses list, so people will click that row _because they
68	saw the note_, and destroy it.
69	
70	Reconciliation gets this right already — `openReceiptEditModal` there
71	(`reconciliation/+page.svelte:350`) fetches the real row with `select('*')`.
72	
73	## Decisions
74	
75	Each was put as a question and answered; the reasoning is kept because the
76	alternatives are not obviously wrong.
77	
78	**A note is human-authored, and the app may only seed it at capture time.** OCR or
79	scan-time extraction may write a note _before_ any person can see the receipt.
80	From the moment a receipt is visible in the app, the note is the family's. There
81	is no `source` column and no author attribution, because the temporal ordering
82	makes conflict impossible: a machine write after a human has seen the receipt is
83	a bug, not a case to model.
84	
85	**Splits copy the note.** `buildSplitReceiptInsert` (`ReceiptService.ts:598`) is an
86	explicit whitelist, so this had to be chosen rather than defaulted. A note is
87	identity ("Sam's birthday"), and the domain model already frames a Split Receipt
88	as a full Receipt inheriting the original's identity — merchant, card, currency
89	and image all carry over. Copying is also the recoverable error: the person opens
90	the split and deletes two sentences. Blanking is unrecoverable, because nothing
91	tells them a note was ever there.
92	
93	**1024 characters, a `<textarea>`, newlines allowed.** Notes will usually be
94	short, but the ceiling costs nothing and the one time someone needs to write out a
95	warranty claim the field should not fight them. A single-line `<input>` for
96	something people will occasionally paste a paragraph into is miserable to edit.
97	
98	**No `maxlength`.** Type and paste freely; a counter appears near the limit and
99	Save is blocked past it with an inline message. `maxlength` **silently truncates a
100	paste** — the person sees text, saves, and never learns the last sentence is gone.
101	That is the one failure here you cannot detect afterwards. Blocking Save puts the
102	choice of what to cut where it belongs.
103	
104	**Preview lives under the merchant name, not in its own column.** `DataTable`'s
105	container is `overflow-x-auto … sm:overflow-visible` (`:108`) — deliberately
106	visible on desktop so category dropdowns are not clipped — so a table that outgrows
107	its width on desktop **overflows with no scrollbar**, and there is no responsive
108	column hiding. Expenses is already at five columns plus a checkbox. A second line
109	in the merchant cell costs nothing on the ~90% of rows with no note, and reads the
110	way you would say it aloud: "Costco, Sam's birthday gift".
111	
112	**Modal only — no note field on manual create.** The counter-argument is real: a
113	Manual Receipt has no image, so merchant/amount/date is everything the app knows
114	and the note would be the only place detail can live. It lost to duplication —
115	the validation story above would have to exist on a second surface, and the table
116	at the top of this document is what happens in this codebase when one thing is
117	maintained in two places. Create, then click the row you just created. If manual
118	entry turns out to be the dominant note-taking case, adding it later is cheap
119	_because_ the validation will already be factored out.
120	
121	## Changes
122	
123	### 1. Migration
124	
125	```sql
126	ALTER TABLE public.receipts ADD COLUMN notes text;
127	ALTER TABLE public.receipts ADD CONSTRAINT receipts_notes_length
128	  CHECK (notes IS NULL OR char_length(notes) <= 1024);
129	COMMENT ON COLUMN public.receipts.notes IS
130	  'Free-text note about the purchase. Human-authored; the app may only write it at
131	   capture time, before anyone can see the receipt. See docs/domain-model.md.';
132	```
133	
134	Nullable, no default. `NULL` means "no note" — the modal normalizes a

Done. Four files, docs only — no code, no migration.

**`docs/plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md`** (new) — the design. Records each decision *with* the alternative it beat, since none were obvious: capture-time-only machine writes, splits copy, textarea with no `maxlength`, preview under the merchant name, modal-only editing. Then six changes, testing, risks, sequencing.

**`docs/domain-model.md`** — added the **Note** term; a new invariant, *"Note authority is time-ordered, not source-tagged"* (why this field needs no `source` column when categorization does); amended **Split Receipt** to say peers take independent copies that diverge; amended the minimum-data rule so a note can't satisfy it.

**`docs/product-backlog.md`** — five entries: the feature, the deferred exports, the live bug, the five-field-list refactor, and the notes-search open question.

**Two things worth your attention:**

**1. The grilling found a live data-loss bug.** Saving a receipt from the **Expenses** page — even with no edits — erases its tax amount, card name, last-4, and **unmatches a reconciled receipt**. The synthetic `ReceiptRow` at `expenses/+page.svelte:524` hard-codes those as null and `handleReceiptSave` writes them back. It predates this feature and no existing test can see it. Logged as 🔴 in Bugs. Sequence steps 3 and 4 of the plan fix it and ship independently of notes — I'd land them first regardless of whether notes ever get built.

**2. Three assumptions, flagged in the doc under *Assumptions made, not decided*** — reverse any of them cheaply:

- **Exports untouched.** Your "CSV and PDF per-receipt page — added to the backlog for later" read most naturally as *both* deferred, so that's what I wrote. If you meant CSV ships now, it's a two-line addition.
- **Naming**: `notes` column, "Note" label and domain term.
- **The `suspicious_date` drift** between the Receipts and Reconciliation patch literals is vestigial, so `buildReceiptPatch` flattens it. You didn't answer that one; `update()` forces the flag anyway, so there's no observable difference today — but if it was deliberate, the helper needs a parameter.

Two branches the grilling never reached, which I decided rather than leave blank: notes are **not** searchable (new capability, not an extension — logged as an open question), and the note does **not** count toward the receipt minimum-data rule.

**1. No — it's still live at HEAD.**

`58df76f` did touch `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` (78 lines), but not that region — grepping its diff for `openReceiptEditModal`, `handleReceiptSave`, `tax:`, `credit_card`, or `matched_transaction_id` returns nothing. That commit's expenses-page changes were the category-assignment extraction. The synthetic row is at `:539` in `git show HEAD:src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` right now. (Everything I read during the grilling was the working tree at/after `58df76f`, so all the line numbers in the design doc are current.)

**2. The `suspicious_date` drift — and I understated it. The Receipts page's line is dead code with a comment that says the opposite of what happens.**

The two patch literals disagree:

```js
// receipts/+page.svelte:227
// #{#dtv2d} Preserve confirmed suspicious_date status
suspicious_date: updatedReceipt.suspicious_date

// reconciliation/+page.svelte:392 — nothing. Field absent.
```

Then `ReceiptService.update` (`:151`):

```js
if ('transaction_date' in safePatch) {
    safePatch.suspicious_date = false;
}
```

Both pages always send `transaction_date` (`:221` and `:387`), it's in `#EDITABLE_FIELDS`, and `in` tests key presence, not value — so a null date still satisfies it. That branch therefore fires on **every** save from **both** pages.

Which means:

- The Receipts page's carefully-passed `suspicious_date` is written into `safePatch`, then **overwritten with `false` one function later**. It never reaches the database.
- The Reconciliation page sends nothing, and `false` is **added** for it.

Both pages write `suspicious_date = false`, always. Identical outcome, so the drift is unobservable — that's the "vestigial" part.

The sharper part: the comment claims to *preserve* the flag, and the code discards it. The behaviour is correct — the domain model's *Suspicious-date authority* invariant says saving through the modal **is** the confirmation action, so clearing on save is intended — but the rule was centralized into `update()` at some point and the page-level field was left behind. Anyone reading `receipts/+page.svelte:227` today would conclude the flag survives a save. It doesn't.

So `buildReceiptPatch` should **omit** `suspicious_date` (matching Reconciliation) and the misleading comment should go with it — `update()` owns that rule, and it's the page-level duplicate that produced the false claim. The one thing this changes: if anyone later removes the forcing in `update()`, the pages would genuinely diverge, so the rule needs to stay in exactly one place.

I've sharpened both docs to say "dead, with an actively misleading comment" rather than "vestigial":

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle — consult them before and during the loop, not after.

When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification — "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists — and survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams — where tests go

A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything — agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?"

## Anti-patterns

- **Implementation-coupled** — mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological** — the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth — a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing** — writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead — one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

1	# Backlog
2	
3	The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
4	refactoring. Everything here is **open**: something a person could pick up.
5	
6	**Completed work is deleted from this file, not annotated.** History lives in git,
7	in [ADRs](adr/) for decisions and rejected paths, in [`prd-done/`](prd-done/) for
8	finished PRDs, and in `CLAUDE.md` for anything that stays true and will bite
9	someone later. When an item lands, salvage any durable lesson into one of those
10	and remove the bullet. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the
11	full detail lives in [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a
12	reference, not a separate to-do list.
13	
14	## Features
15	
16	- **Spending Report — remaining slices.** The report ships: table + chart views, cell drill-down, editable hierarchy, assign-on-create, and historical-expense import are all live. Still open, roughly in priority order: **chart-bar drill-down** (the same drill affordance the table cells have — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); **prior-period overlay + year-over-year** (unblocked now that historical years can be imported); quarter/period selection; multi-chart menu; export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
17	- **Receipt notes.** A free-text field on the Receipt (max 1024 chars) so a person can record why a purchase mattered — the only field on a Receipt in their own words rather than extracted or inferred. Editable in the receipt edit modal only; previewed truncated under the merchant name on the Receipts and Expenses lists. Fully designed in [Receipt Notes](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md), not built. **Sequence steps 3 and 4 of that plan are independently shippable and worth landing first** — step 4 fixes the live Expenses-page data-loss bug below.
18	- **Receipt notes in the exports.** Deferred from the design above. **CSV** is ~2 lines — one header entry plus one `escapeCSVField` call in `CSVExportService.buildRow` (`:79`); escaping already handles commas, quotes and newlines, and `parseExpenseImportCsv` ignores columns it does not need, so re-import is unaffected. The column appends after Category, so existing spreadsheet formulas on A–D are untouched. **PDF per-receipt page** is one line under the existing reference header (`PDFExportService.ts:470`, `:506`) — the page where you are already looking at the receipt itself. The PDF **summary table** was rejected rather than deferred: fixed column x-positions (`:49`) on an already-tight roll-up, for a detail field that does not belong in a spend summary.
19	- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
20	- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account. This interacts with the unverified-alias security item below — verification is the fix, so design them together.
21	- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped self-insert policy). The read-only half already shipped — the Profile page lists family members via the `get_family_members()` RPC — so what remains is invite / accept / remove.
22	- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). One on-device check is still outstanding: HEIC is now decoded and transcoded to JPEG like everything else (see [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md)), but nobody has confirmed what an iPhone actually hands over, or that Safari decodes it as expected — if it doesn't, the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is now refused rather than silently uploaded full-size.
23	- **Vendor-rule management UI.** Vendor rules are created silently — on first categorization, and (once the design above lands) applied by a database trigger — but **nothing in the app lists them**. There is no way to see which rules exist, correct one, or delete a bad one. Sharpened by the junk-rule item under Correctness below: garbled OCR merchant names create patterns that never match again, and today they are invisible and unremovable.
24	- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y** _(optional UX, low priority)_. A recent-categories section in the dropdown, a mobile-responsive category dropdown, and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support were specced but never built.
25	- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits** _(optional, low priority)_. The read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal.
26	
27	## Bugs / UX issues
28	
29	- **🔴 Saving a receipt from the Expenses page erases tax, card details and the reconciliation match.** _(Found 2026-08-03 during the Receipt Notes design.)_ `openReceiptEditModal` (`src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte:524`) builds a **synthetic `ReceiptRow`** from the `Expense` projection, hard-coding every field `Expense` does not carry — `tax: null`, `credit_card_name: null`, `credit_card_last_4: null`, `matched_transaction_id: null`, `suspicious_date: false` (`:533`–`:541`). `handleReceiptSave` (`:550`) then writes all of them back (`:559`–`:566`). So opening any receipt from the **Expenses** page, changing nothing and pressing Save destroys its tax amount, card name and last-4 — and **unmatches a reconciled receipt**. `matched_transaction_id` is the sharpest case: `Expense` genuinely carries it (`ExpenseService.ts:31`) and the synthetic row discards it anyway. The Receipts and Reconciliation pages are unaffected — Reconciliation fetches the real row with `select('*')` (`reconciliation/+page.svelte:350`), which is the fix. **This is a class, not an instance:** every column added to `receipts` from now on inherits it, silently. Fix and regression test are step 4 of [Receipt Notes](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md) (`ReceiptService.getById` + stop synthesizing) and ship independently of that feature. No existing test can see this.
30	- **Receipt with no date is hard to find.** If a receipt has no date it is hard to locate in the receipts view.
31	- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
32	- **Split receipts: decide what a split inherits.** Punted 2026-08-03 during the design above. `splitReceipt` copies the original's merchant into a new receipt row, so once the vendor-rule trigger exists a split will get **the merchant's rule** — even when the parent was manually reclassified away from it. That is an unexamined default, not a decision. The alternatives are inheriting the parent's current category (most recent human signal about that purchase) or leaving splits deliberately uncategorized (you split _because_ the halves differ). Needs its own design pass.

### 5. The Expenses page stops synthesizing a receipt

`ReceiptService` gains `getById(id)` — a `select('*').eq('id', id).single()`, which
is what the Reconciliation page already does inline (`:354`) and what
`fetchOriginalForSplit` (`:565`) does privately. Both should be moved onto it.

`openReceiptEditModal` on the Expenses page awaits `getById` and passes the real
row to the modal, replacing the synthetic literal at `:526`–`:542`. One extra
round-trip on row click, on a click that already opens a modal and fetches a signed
image URL.

This removes the whole class of defect rather than the instance: every field added
to `receipts` from now on inherits the bug otherwise, `notes` being the next one.

Chosen over adding `notes` to the `Expense` projection and threading it into the
synthetic row, which would have made notes safe while tax, card details and the
reconciliation match kept being erased — and widened the pattern that caused it.

### 6. Splits

`buildSplitReceiptInsert` gains `notes: original.notes`.

While in there: `original_filename` is **not** in that whitelist, so a split
silently loses its filename today. Same class, one line. Out of scope here but
worth a look while the file is open.

`suspicious_date: true` would survive and the assertion would fail.

the page genuinely fetches one.

content.content:
17:- **Receipt notes.** A free-text field on the Receipt (max 1024 chars) so a person can record why a purchase mattered — the only field on a Receipt in their own words rather than extracted or inferred. Editable in the receipt edit modal only; previewed truncated under the merchant name on the Receipts and Expenses lists. Fully designed in [Receipt Notes](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md), not built. **Sequence steps 3 and 4 of that plan are independently shippable and worth landing first** — step 4 fixes the live Expenses-page data-loss bug below.
29:- **🔴 Saving a receipt from the Expenses page erases tax, card details and the reconciliation match.** _(Found 2026-08-03 during the Receipt Notes design.)_ `openReceiptEditModal` (`src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte:524`) builds a **synthetic `ReceiptRow`** from the `Expense` projection, hard-coding every field `Expense` does not carry — `tax: null`, `credit_card_name: null`, `credit_card_last_4: null`, `matched_transaction_id: null`, `suspicious_date: false` (`:533`–`:541`). `handleReceiptSave` (`:550`) then writes all of them back (`:559`–`:566`). So opening any receipt from the **Expenses** page, changing nothing and pressing Save destroys its tax amount, card name and last-4 — and **unmatches a reconciled receipt**. `matched_transaction_id` is the sharpest case: `Expense` genuinely carries it (`ExpenseService.ts:31`) and the synthetic row discards it anyway. The Receipts and Reconciliation pages are unaffected — Reconciliation fetches the real row with `select('*')` (`reconciliation/+page.svelte:350`), which is the fix. **This is a class, not an instance:** every column added to `receipts` from now on inherits it, silently. Fix and regression test are step 4 of [Receipt Notes](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md) (`ReceiptService.getById` + stop synthesizing) and ship independently of that feature. No existing test can see this.
80:- **Five hand-maintained receipt field lists, already drifting.** Adding one column to `receipts` means editing five places the compiler cannot check: `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (`:118`), three page-level patch literals (`receipts/+page.svelte:218`, `reconciliation/+page.svelte:384`, `expenses/+page.svelte:555`), and `isDirty` in `ReceiptEditModal.svelte:68`. Miss the first four and the field silently never persists — no error; miss the fifth and closing a modal discards an unsaved edit with no prompt. They have **already drifted**: the Receipts patch carries `suspicious_date` (`:228`), Reconciliation's does not (`:392`) — and the Receipts one is **dead code under a comment that says the opposite of what happens**. `ReceiptService.update` sets `suspicious_date = false` whenever `transaction_date` is present in the patch (`:151`); both pages always send it, so the value passed under _"Preserve confirmed suspicious_date status"_ (`:227`) is overwritten before it reaches the database and has never had any effect. The behaviour is correct (see the _Suspicious-date authority_ invariant in [Domain model](domain-model.md)) — the rule was centralized into `update()` and the page-level copy was left behind. Extracting one `buildReceiptPatch(row)` takes five down to three; it is step 3 of [Receipt Notes](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md) and is a pure refactor that ships on its own.
81:- **`splitReceipt` silently drops `original_filename`.** `buildSplitReceiptInsert` (`ReceiptService.ts:598`) is an explicit whitelist and does not list it, so a Split Receipt loses the name its Source File arrived under while inheriting merchant, card, currency and image. One line. Same class as the field-list item above — noticed 2026-08-03 while deciding whether splits inherit the new Note (they do).

- **`ReceiptService` ships debug logging to production.** Three `console.log`s on the receipts-page load path (`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:84`, `:91`, `:101`) print the user id, the **full `family_members` rows for that user**, and the fetched receipt payload to the browser console on every visit. 1	# Receipt Notes — Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-03
4	**Status:** 📋 Designed. **The notes feature itself is not built** — but the two live
5	bugs this design uncovered are fixed and covered by tests: §5 (the Expenses page no
6	longer synthesizes a receipt) and the `original_filename` half of §6 both landed
7	2026-08-03, ahead of any notes work, because neither depends on it. Decisions below
8	were settled in a grilling session the same day; the open items are marked inline as
9	[assumptions](#assumptions-made-not-decided).
10	
11	A Receipt records merchant, amount and date, and nothing else a person can say in
12	their own words. Everything else the app knows is either extracted from the image
13	or inferred. So there is nowhere to write down _"Sam's birthday gift"_,
14	_"reimbursable — client dinner"_, or _"warranty runs to 2028"_ — the reasons a
15	purchase actually mattered.
16	
17	This adds one free-text field to the Receipt, editable in the receipt edit modal,
18	with a truncated preview on the Receipts and Expenses lists.
19	
20	It is a small feature that lands on top of a real bug. Adding a column to
21	`receipts` means touching **five hand-maintained field lists**, none of which the
22	compiler checks — and one of the five is a synthetic `ReceiptRow` on the Expenses
23	page that is **already silently destroying data in production**. That fix is in
24	scope, because notes walk straight into it.
25	
26	## What exists today
27	
28	`receipts` has no note-like column (`supabase/migrations/20260726120000_baseline.sql:595`)
29	and nothing in `Receipt.ts` is close. `ReceiptEditModal` (shared by the Receipts,
30	Expenses and Reconciliation pages) edits nine fields; both list pages render an
31	explicit `DataTable` `columns` array (`receipts/+page.svelte:908`,
32	`expenses/+page.svelte:1220`).
33	
34	### The five field lists
35	
36	| #   | Location                                                    | Silent failure if `notes` is omitted                                      |
37	| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
38	| 1   | `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (`ReceiptService.ts:118`) | `update()` strips the field. No error, no save.                           |
39	| 2   | patch literal, Receipts page (`+page.svelte:218`)           | Note never saves from Receipts                                            |
40	| 3   | patch literal, Reconciliation page (`+page.svelte:384`)     | Note never saves from Reconciliation                                      |
41	| 4   | patch literal, Expenses page (`+page.svelte:555`)           | Note never saves from Expenses                                            |
42	| 5   | `isDirty` in the modal (`ReceiptEditModal.svelte:68`)       | Closing with an unsaved note gives **no warning** — the note is discarded |
43	
44	All five are inferred object literals or a string `Set`, so omitting a field
45	type-checks cleanly. They have already drifted: the Receipts patch carries
46	`suspicious_date` (`:228`) and the Reconciliation patch does not (`:392`).
47	
48	### The bug this feature would have inherited
49	
50	`openReceiptEditModal` on the Expenses page (`expenses/+page.svelte:524`) builds a
51	**synthetic `ReceiptRow`** from the `Expense` projection, hard-coding every field
52	`Expense` does not carry:
53	
54	```js
55	tax: null,
56	credit_card_name: null,
57	credit_card_last_4: null,
58	matched_transaction_id: null,   // Expense DOES carry this — it is discarded anyway
59	suspicious_date: false,
60	```
61	
62	`handleReceiptSave` (`:550`) then writes all of them back (`:559`–`:566`).
63	
64	**Open any receipt from the Expenses page, change nothing, press Save — and you
65	erase its tax amount, card name, last-4 digits, and its reconciliation match.** A
66	receipt matched to a TD transaction becomes unmatched. This is live today and
67	predates this feature.
68	
69	`notes` would have joined that list, and worse: the whole point of §4 below is to
70	show the note on the Expenses list, so people will click that row _because they
71	saw the note_, and destroy it.
72	
73	Reconciliation gets this right already — `openReceiptEditModal` there
74	(`reconciliation/+page.svelte:350`) fetches the real row with `select('*')`.
75	
76	## Decisions
77	
78	Each was put as a question and answered; the reasoning is kept because the
79	alternatives are not obviously wrong.
80	
81	**A note is human-authored, and the app may only seed it at capture time.** OCR or
82	scan-time extraction may write a note _before_ any person can see the receipt.
83	From the moment a receipt is visible in the app, the note is the family's. There
84	is no `source` column and no author attribution, because the temporal ordering
85	makes conflict impossible: a machine write after a human has seen the receipt is
86	a bug, not a case to model.
87	
88	**Splits copy the note.** `buildSplitReceiptInsert` (`ReceiptService.ts:598`) is an
89	explicit whitelist, so this had to be chosen rather than defaulted. A note is
90	identity ("Sam's birthday"), and the domain model already frames a Split Receipt
91	as a full Receipt inheriting the original's identity — merchant, card, currency
92	and image all carry over. Copying is also the recoverable error: the person opens
93	the split and deletes two sentences. Blanking is unrecoverable, because nothing
94	tells them a note was ever there.
95	
96	**1024 characters, a `<textarea>`, newlines allowed.** Notes will usually be
97	short, but the ceiling costs nothing and the one time someone needs to write out a
98	warranty claim the field should not fight them. A single-line `<input>` for
99	something people will occasionally paste a paragraph into is miserable to edit.
100	
101	**No `maxlength`.** Type and paste freely; a counter appears near the limit and
102	Save is blocked past it with an inline message. `maxlength` **silently truncates a
103	paste** — the person sees text, saves, and never learns the last sentence is gone.
104	That is the one failure here you cannot detect afterwards. Blocking Save puts the
105	choice of what to cut where it belongs.
106	
107	**Preview lives under the merchant name, not in its own column.** `DataTable`'s
108	container is `overflow-x-auto … sm:overflow-visible` (`:108`) — deliberately

111	column hiding. Expenses is already at five columns plus a checkbox. A second line

115	**Modal only — no note field on manual create.** The counter-argument is real: a
116	Manual Receipt has no image, so merchant/amount/date is everything the app knows
117	and the note would be the only place detail can live. It lost to duplication —
118	the validation story above would have to exist on a second surface, and the table

120	maintained in two places. Create, then click the row you just created. If manual
121	entry turns out to be the dominant note-taking case, adding it later is cheap

-- A free-text Note on a Receipt.
--
-- The one field on a Receipt written in a person's own words rather than
-- extracted from the image or inferred. "Sam's birthday gift", "reimbursable —
-- client dinner", "warranty runs to 2028".
--
-- Authority is time-ordered, not source-tagged: the app may write a note at
-- capture time (during upload or scan, before anyone can see the Receipt), and
-- from the moment the Receipt is visible the note belongs to the family. The two
-- writers can never contend, which is why there is no source column, no author
-- and no history here. A machine write after a person has seen the Receipt is a
-- bug, not a case this schema models.
--
-- Design: docs/plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md
-- Glossary + invariant: docs/domain-model.md

ALTER TABLE "public"."receipts" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "notes" "text";

-- The real limit. Client-side validation in the edit modal is UX only — three
-- write paths never touch it (email ingestion in supabase/functions/, the
-- historical importer, and capture-time seeding), and any of them could grow a
-- note-writing branch later.
--
-- char_length() counts characters, not bytes, so 1024 emoji are 1024 characters.
-- The browser's UTF-16 .length over-counts astral characters, which makes the
-- client check conservative: it can never admit something this constraint rejects.
ALTER TABLE "public"."receipts"
	ADD CONSTRAINT "receipts_notes_length"

-- A free-text Note on a Receipt.
--
-- The one field on a Receipt written in a person's own words rather than
-- extracted from the image or inferred. "Sam's birthday gift", "reimbursable —
-- client dinner", "warranty runs to 2028".
--
-- Authority is time-ordered, not source-tagged: the app may write a note at
-- capture time (during upload or scan, before anyone can see the Receipt), and
-- from the moment the Receipt is visible the note belongs to the family. The two
-- writers can never contend, which is why there is no source column, no author
-- and no history here. A machine write after a person has seen the Receipt is a
-- bug, not a case this schema models.
--
-- Design: docs/plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md
-- Glossary + invariant: docs/domain-model.md

ALTER TABLE "public"."receipts" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "notes" "text";

-- The real limit. Client-side validation in the edit modal is UX only — three
-- write paths never touch it (email ingestion in supabase/functions/, the
-- historical importer, and capture-time seeding), and any of them could grow a
-- note-writing branch later.
--
-- char_length() counts characters, not bytes, so 1024 emoji are 1024 characters.
-- The browser's UTF-16 .length over-counts astral characters, which makes the
-- client check conservative: it can never admit something this constraint rejects.
ALTER TABLE "public"."receipts"
	ADD CONSTRAINT "receipts_notes_length"
	CHECK ("notes" IS NULL OR "char_length"("notes") <= 1024);

COMMENT ON COLUMN "public"."receipts"."notes" IS
	'Free-text Note about the purchase, in the family''s own words. Human-authored; the app may write it only at capture time, before anyone can see the Receipt. NULL means no note — never the empty string. Max 1024 chars (receipts_notes_length). See docs/domain-model.md.';
