1	# Backlog
2	
3	The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
4	refactoring. Everything here is **open**: something a person could pick up.
5	
6	**Completed work is deleted from this file, not annotated.** History lives in git,
7	in [ADRs](adr/) for decisions and rejected paths, in [`prd-done/`](prd-done/) for
8	finished PRDs, and in `CLAUDE.md` for anything that stays true and will bite
9	someone later. When an item lands, salvage any durable lesson into one of those
10	and remove the bullet. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the
11	full detail lives in [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a
12	reference, not a separate to-do list.
13	
14	## Features
15	
16	- **Spending Report — remaining slices.** The report ships: table + chart views, cell drill-down, editable hierarchy, assign-on-create, and historical-expense import are all live. Still open, roughly in priority order: **chart-bar drill-down** (the same drill affordance the table cells have — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); **prior-period overlay + year-over-year** (unblocked now that historical years can be imported); quarter/period selection; multi-chart menu; export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
17	- **Receipt notes.** A free-text field on the Receipt (max 1024 chars) so a person can record why a purchase mattered — the only field on a Receipt in their own words rather than extracted or inferred. Editable in the receipt edit modal only; previewed truncated under the merchant name on the Receipts and Expenses lists. Fully designed in [Receipt Notes](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-notes-design.md), not built. The two bugs that design uncovered — the Expenses page erasing tax/card/match on save, and `splitReceipt` dropping `original_filename` — are **already fixed and tested**, ahead of the feature, since neither needed the column.
18	- **Receipt notes in the exports.** Deferred from the design above. **CSV** is ~2 lines — one header entry plus one `escapeCSVField` call in `CSVExportService.buildRow` (`:79`); escaping already handles commas, quotes and newlines, and `parseExpenseImportCsv` ignores columns it does not need, so re-import is unaffected. The column appends after Category, so existing spreadsheet formulas on A–D are untouched. **PDF per-receipt page** is one line under the existing reference header (`PDFExportService.ts:470`, `:506`) — the page where you are already looking at the receipt itself. The PDF **summary table** was rejected rather than deferred: fixed column x-positions (`:49`) on an already-tight roll-up, for a detail field that does not belong in a spend summary.
19	- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
20	- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account. This interacts with the unverified-alias security item below — verification is the fix, so design them together.
21	- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped self-insert policy). The read-only half already shipped — the Profile page lists family members via the `get_family_members()` RPC — so what remains is invite / accept / remove.
22	- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). One on-device check is still outstanding: HEIC is now decoded and transcoded to JPEG like everything else (see [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md)), but nobody has confirmed what an iPhone actually hands over, or that Safari decodes it as expected — if it doesn't, the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is now refused rather than silently uploaded full-size.
23	- **Vendor-rule management UI.** Vendor rules are created silently — on first categorization, and (once the design above lands) applied by a database trigger — but **nothing in the app lists them**. There is no way to see which rules exist, correct one, or delete a bad one. Sharpened by the junk-rule item under Correctness below: garbled OCR merchant names create patterns that never match again, and today they are invisible and unremovable.
24	- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y** _(optional UX, low priority)_. A recent-categories section in the dropdown, a mobile-responsive category dropdown, and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support were specced but never built.
25	- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits** _(optional, low priority)_. The read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal.
26	
27	## Bugs / UX issues
28	
29	- **Receipt with no date is hard to find.** If a receipt has no date it is hard to locate in the receipts view.
30	- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
31	- **Split receipts: decide what a split inherits.** Punted 2026-08-03 during the design above. `splitReceipt` copies the original's merchant into a new receipt row, so once the vendor-rule trigger exists a split will get **the merchant's rule** — even when the parent was manually reclassified away from it. That is an unexamined default, not a decision. The alternatives are inheriting the parent's current category (most recent human signal about that purchase) or leaving splits deliberately uncategorized (you split _because_ the halves differ). Needs its own design pass.
32	- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
33	- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.

import type { ReceiptRow, ReceiptInsert } from '$lib/models/Receipt';

/**
 * A Note's empty value is `NULL`, never `''`.
 *
 * A textarea hands back `''` when cleared and `'  '` when someone types a space
 * and thinks better of it. Letting either reach the database would give "no note"
 * three spellings, and every reader — the list preview, the dirty check, a future
 * export — would have to know all three.
 */
export function normalizeNote(notes: string | null | undefined): string | null {
	const trimmed = notes?.trim();
	return trimmed ? trimmed : null;
}

/**
 * The patch `ReceiptEditModal` sends to `ReceiptService.update`, from the edited
 * row.
 *
 * One definition for all three pages that host the modal. They each hand-wrote
 * this list before, and the lists had already drifted — the Receipts one carried
 * `suspicious_date` and Reconciliation's did not — which is exactly how a newly
 * added column ends up saving from two pages out of three, silently and with no
 * error.
 *
 * Deliberately narrow: **only the fields the modal can actually change**.
 * `receipt_image_path` and `matched_transaction_id` were in the Expenses page's
 * patch but are not editable here, and writing back a value the modal only ever
 * read turns any save into a lost update if someone else reconciled that receipt
 * meanwhile.
 *
 * `suspicious_date` is absent on purpose. `ReceiptService.update` sets it to false
 * whenever `transaction_date` is present, because saving through the modal *is*
 * the date-confirmation action (see the Suspicious-date authority invariant in
 * docs/domain-model.md). That rule lives there and nowhere else.
 */
export function buildReceiptPatch(receipt: ReceiptRow): ReceiptInsert {
	return {
		merchant_name: receipt.merchant_name,
		transaction_date: receipt.transaction_date,
		total_amount: receipt.total_amount,
		tax: receipt.tax,
		currency: receipt.currency,
		exchange_rate_to_cad: receipt.exchange_rate_to_cad,
		credit_card_name: receipt.credit_card_name,
		credit_card_last_4: receipt.credit_card_last_4,
		notes: normalizeNote(receipt.notes)
	};
}

1	# Receipt Notes — Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-03
4	**Status:** ✅ Built 2026-08-03 (pending release) — `receipts.notes` + CHECK, the
5	`Note (optional)` textarea with counter and save-gating, previews on both list pages,
6	splits copying the note, and `buildReceiptPatch` replacing the three page-level patch
7	literals. The two live bugs this design uncovered (§5 and the `original_filename` half
8	of §6) were fixed first, ahead of the feature.
9	
10	**One verification step outstanding:** `npm run db:reset` has **not** been run against
11	the migration — Docker was not available. CLAUDE.md requires it before pushing.
12	
13	Decisions below were settled in a grilling session on 2026-08-03; deferred items are
14	listed under [Deferred](#deferred).
15	
16	A Receipt records merchant, amount and date, and nothing else a person can say in
17	their own words. Everything else the app knows is either extracted from the image
18	or inferred. So there is nowhere to write down _"Sam's birthday gift"_,
19	_"reimbursable — client dinner"_, or _"warranty runs to 2028"_ — the reasons a
20	purchase actually mattered.
21	
22	This adds one free-text field to the Receipt, editable in the receipt edit modal,
23	with a truncated preview on the Receipts and Expenses lists.
24	
25	It is a small feature that landed on top of a real bug. Adding a column to
26	`receipts` means touching **five hand-maintained field lists**, none of which the
27	compiler checks — and one of the five was a synthetic `ReceiptRow` on the Expenses
28	page that had been **silently destroying data in production**. Designing notes is
29	what surfaced it, so it was fixed first; see §5.
30	
31	## What exists today
32	
33	`receipts` has no note-like column (`supabase/migrations/20260726120000_baseline.sql:595`)
34	and nothing in `Receipt.ts` is close. `ReceiptEditModal` (shared by the Receipts,
35	Expenses and Reconciliation pages) edits nine fields; both list pages render an
36	explicit `DataTable` `columns` array (`receipts/+page.svelte:908`,
37	`expenses/+page.svelte:1220`).

39	### The five field lists
40	
41	| #   | Location                                                    | Silent failure if `notes` is omitted                                      |
42	| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
43	| 1   | `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (`ReceiptService.ts:118`) | `update()` strips the field. No error, no save.                           |
44	| 2   | patch literal, Receipts page (`+page.svelte:218`)           | Note never saves from Receipts                                            |
45	| 3   | patch literal, Reconciliation page (`+page.svelte:384`)     | Note never saves from Reconciliation                                      |
46	| 4   | patch literal, Expenses page (`+page.svelte:555`)           | Note never saves from Expenses                                            |
47	| 5   | `isDirty` in the modal (`ReceiptEditModal.svelte:68`)       | Closing with an unsaved note gives **no warning** — the note is discarded |
48	
49	All five are inferred object literals or a string `Set`, so omitting a field
50	type-checks cleanly. They have already drifted: the Receipts patch carries
51	`suspicious_date` (`:228`) and the Reconciliation patch does not (`:392`).
52	
53	### The bug this feature would have inherited — fixed, described as it was found
54	
55	`openReceiptEditModal` on the Expenses page (`expenses/+page.svelte:524`) builds a
56	**synthetic `ReceiptRow`** from the `Expense` projection, hard-coding every field
57	`Expense` does not carry:
58	
59	```js

61	credit_card_name: null,
62	credit_card_last_4: null,
63	matched_transaction_id: null,   // Expense DOES carry this — it is discarded anyway
64	suspicious_date: false,
65	```
66	
67	`handleReceiptSave` (`:550`) then writes all of them back (`:559`–`:566`).
68	
69	**Open any receipt from the Expenses page, change nothing, press Save — and you
70	erased its tax amount, card name, last-4 digits, and its reconciliation match.** A
71	receipt matched to a TD transaction became unmatched. This predated the feature and
72	had been live since the modal was wired to the Expenses page. Fixed in §5.
73	
74	`notes` would have joined that list, and worse: the whole point of §4 below is to
75	show the note on the Expenses list, so people will click that row _because they
76	saw the note_, and destroy it.
77	
78	Reconciliation gets this right already — `openReceiptEditModal` there
79	(`reconciliation/+page.svelte:350`) fetches the real row with `select('*')`.
80	
81	## Decisions
82	
83	Each was put as a question and answered; the reasoning is kept because the
84	alternatives are not obviously wrong.
85	
86	**A note is human-authored, and the app may only seed it at capture time.** OCR or
87	scan-time extraction may write a note _before_ any person can see the receipt.
88	From the moment a receipt is visible in the app, the note is the family's. There
89	is no `source` column and no author attribution, because the temporal ordering
90	makes conflict impossible: a machine write after a human has seen the receipt is
91	a bug, not a case to model.
92	
93	**Splits copy the note.** `buildSplitReceiptInsert` (`ReceiptService.ts:598`) is an
94	explicit whitelist, so this had to be chosen rather than defaulted. A note is
95	identity ("Sam's birthday"), and the domain model already frames a Split Receipt
96	as a full Receipt inheriting the original's identity — merchant, card, currency
97	and image all carry over. Copying is also the recoverable error: the person opens
98	the split and deletes two sentences. Blanking is unrecoverable, because nothing
99	tells them a note was ever there.
100	
101	**1024 characters, a `<textarea>`, newlines allowed.** Notes will usually be
102	short, but the ceiling costs nothing and the one time someone needs to write out a
103	warranty claim the field should not fight them. A single-line `<input>` for
104	something people will occasionally paste a paragraph into is miserable to edit.
105	
106	**No `maxlength`.** Type and paste freely; a counter appears near the limit and
107	Save is blocked past it with an inline message. `maxlength` **silently truncates a
108	paste** — the person sees text, saves, and never learns the last sentence is gone.
109	That is the one failure here you cannot detect afterwards. Blocking Save puts the
110	choice of what to cut where it belongs.
111	
112	**Preview lives under the merchant name, not in its own column.** `DataTable`'s
113	container is `overflow-x-auto … sm:overflow-visible` (`:108`) — deliberately
114	visible on desktop so category dropdowns are not clipped — so a table that outgrows
115	its width on desktop **overflows with no scrollbar**, and there is no responsive
116	column hiding. Expenses is already at five columns plus a checkbox. A second line
117	in the merchant cell costs nothing on the ~90% of rows with no note, and reads the
118	way you would say it aloud: "Costco, Sam's birthday gift".
119	
120	**Modal only — no note field on manual create.** The counter-argument is real: a
121	Manual Receipt has no image, so merchant/amount/date is everything the app knows
122	and the note would be the only place detail can live. It lost to duplication —
123	the validation story above would have to exist on a second surface, and the table
124	at the top of this document is what happens in this codebase when one thing is
125	maintained in two places. Create, then click the row you just created. If manual
126	entry turns out to be the dominant note-taking case, adding it later is cheap
127	_because_ the validation will already be factored out.

content.content: 67:- **Auto-categorization is applied by the database, not the client.** The `apply_vendor_rule_after_insert` trigger on `receipts` assigns the family's vendor-rule category (`source='auto'`, only when no `expense_categories` row exists). **Do not reintroduce client-side assignment** — `ReceiptService.autoAssignCategoryBestEffort` was deleted precisely because it only ever covered browser upload, leaving manual entry, splits, the historical importer, and email ingestion uncategorized. The trigger is best-effort by design (it swallows its own errors) so a categorization failure can never abort receipt creation. `applyAllVendorRules` still runs on Expenses **and** Receipts page load, but only as a retroactive net: a rule created after a receipt exists fans out solely over the rows that were on screen at the time. Normalization is lowercase → trim → strip non-alphanumerics → collapse whitespace, and that order is load-bearing (trimming last would change the result).

- **Auto-categorization is applied by the database, not the client.** The `apply_vendor_rule_after_insert` trigger on `receipts` assigns the family's vendor-rule category (`source='auto'`, only when no `expense_categories` row exists). **Do not reintroduce client-side assignment** — `ReceiptService.autoAssignCategoryBestEffort` was deleted precisely because it only ever covered browser upload, leaving manual entry, splits, the historical importer, and email ingestion uncategorized. The trigger is best-effort by design (it swallows its own errors) so a categorization failure can never abort receipt creation. `applyAllVendorRules` still runs on Expenses **and** Receipts page load, but only as a retroactive net: a rule created after a receipt exists fans out solely over the rows that were on screen at the time. Related trap: **SQL `normalize_vendor()` must match `ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` exactly** — `vendor_pattern` is stored already-normalized, so drift raises no error and rules just silently stop matching. Both are pinned to the shared list in `src/lib/utils/vendorNormalizationCases.ts`; the SQL half is only checked by `npm run test:integration`, which needs a live stack and gates nothing. Normalization is lowercase → trim → strip non-alphanumerics → collapse whitespace, and that order is load-bearing (trimming last would change the result).

- **Date pickers use flowbite-svelte.** Always use `<Datepicker>` from `flowbite-svelte` with `toDate()` and `toISODateString()` helpers from `$lib/utils/dateConversion`. Never use raw `<input type="date">`.

- **Never use `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD")` for date-only strings.** JavaScript parses bare date strings as UTC midnight, which shifts to the previous day in timezones west of UTC. Always use `toDate()` to parse or `formatDate()` to display — both from `$lib/utils/dateConversion`. These parse year/month/day parts manually to construct local-time Date objects.

Two different things are bundled in that question, and they have opposite answers.

**`npm run dev` points at the *local* stack, not production** — `dev` → `local:env` → `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321`. (`dev:remote` is the one that hits the real project.) And the local database gets its schema by **replaying `supabase/migrations/`**.

**So: yes, you can run dev with the migration uncommitted.** `supabase db reset` reads your working tree, not git. Git is not involved in applying schema. You need Docker up:

```
npm run db:up        # supabase start
npm run db:reset     # replays migrations incl. the new one — also the CLAUDE.md verification step
npm run dev
```

`db:reset` is destructive to local data. If you'd rather keep your local rows, `supabase migration up` applies only pending migrations — but run the full `db:reset` at least once before pushing, since that's what proves the migration replays from scratch.

**But never committing it is a different proposition, and it breaks production.** The column has to exist in whatever database the app talks to, and the migration file is the only thing that puts it there. Without it:

- **The Expenses page breaks outright** — `ExpenseService.getExpenses` names `notes` in its `select`, so PostgREST 400s on the unknown column and the whole query throws. Not a missing note: no expenses at all.
- The Receipts page degrades quietly instead — `ReceiptService.list` uses `select('*')`, which tolerates the column being absent, so rows render and notes just never appear. Saving one then 400s.

And this repo has already paid for exactly this. CLAUDE.md records why the migrations were squashed to a baseline: `families` was created **by hand in the dashboard** and only captured later by a schema dump, so a from-scratch replay died at `007` with `relation "public.families" does not exist`. A column that exists in a database but not in `supabase/migrations/` is that same defect in miniature.

If what you actually want is to **try the feature before deciding whether to keep it**, the clean shape is: keep the migration file (uncommitted is fine), run it locally, and `git checkout` the whole change if you don't like it. If you want to **commit the app code now and the migration later**, don't — that ordering deploys a build whose Expenses page is broken until the migration lands.

Got it — that inverts the risk entirely. Straight answer: **yes, that works, and the ordering is actually the safe one.**

`supabase db push` reads your working tree and applies to the linked remote, recording the filename in the remote `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` table. Git is not involved. Then `npm run dev:remote` (`op run --env-file=.env -- vite dev`) runs the app against that same live project, so the column is there and the feature works end to end.

The schema change is backwards-compatible, which is what makes the ordering fine: a **nullable** column plus a CHECK that only constrains non-null values. The currently-deployed code never mentions `notes`, and `select('*')` tolerates a new column, so pushing the migration before the app code breaks nothing. Additive-then-deploy is the correct sequence.

Three cautions, in order of how much they'd actually bite:

**1. `dev:remote` writes to real family data.** This isn't a read-only spin. Every Save in the modal now goes through `buildReceiptPatch`, which changed what *all three pages* send — not just notes. Testing it against the live project means real receipts get patched by code that has never run against real data. If you want to exercise the 1025-character rejection or the whitespace normalization, do it on a receipt you don't mind editing.

**2. `db push` applies *every* pending migration, not just this one.** Check what it's about to do first:

```
supabase migration list          # local vs remote
supabase db push --dry-run
```

If `20260803_apply_vendor_rules_on_receipt_insert.sql` hasn't been pushed yet, it goes up in the same operation — and that one installs a trigger, which is a much bigger change than adding a column.

**3. Pushed-but-uncommitted is the drift direction that's hardest to repair.** Once pushed, the remote migration history has a row naming `20260803120000_receipt_notes.sql`. If that file never reaches git, any fresh checkout — another machine, a clean clone, `npm run db:reset` locally — has a database that can't reproduce prod, and a remote history entry pointing at a file nobody has. That is precisely the failure CLAUDE.md records: `families` made by hand in the dashboard, captured only later by a dump, replay dying at `007`, prod history "repaired to match (bookkeeping only)".

So: push it and test against remote if you like — but commit the `.sql` with the app code rather than never. The thing you can safely skip is `npm run db:reset`; pushing to remote and exercising it there is a legitimate substitute for verifying the migration, arguably a better one since it runs against real data volumes.

That table has **four** rows but only **three** migrations — rows 2 and 4 are the same file, shown twice because the CLI can't pair it.

The `Time (UTC)` column is the tell. The baseline renders as `2026-07-26 12:00:00`; the `20260803` rows render as the raw string `20260803`. The CLI parses migration versions as 14-digit `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`, and `20260803_apply_vendor_rules_on_receipt_insert.sql` is only **8 digits**, so it can't parse it, can't match local against remote, and lists it once on each side.

Reading it correctly:

| Row | What it actually is |
|---|---|
| `20260726120000` ↔ `20260726120000` | Baseline, in sync ✓ |
| ` ` \| `20260803` | Vendor-rules trigger — **is** applied to prod |
| `20260803120000` \| ` ` | My notes migration — genuinely pending ✓ |
| `20260803` \| ` ` | Same vendor-rules file, unpaired |

**So only one migration is truly pending — mine.** But because the CLI thinks `20260803` is local-only, `db push` will likely try to re-apply it.

**That happens to be safe.** I checked: `create or replace function` for both functions, `drop trigger if exists` before `create trigger`, and the one `insert` is inside the trigger function's body, not top-level DML. Re-running redefines the function and trigger and touches no data. That's luck rather than design, but it holds.

Two things not to do:

- **Don't rename that file to 14 digits.** It's recorded on remote as `20260803`. Renaming makes it look like a brand-new migration that gets applied under a new version, while the old remote entry is orphaned — strictly worse than the current cosmetic confusion.
- **Don't push blind.** `supabase db push --dry-run` will tell you whether it plans to re-run `20260803` or just apply mine.

The root cause is a documentation bug: **CLAUDE.md states the convention as `YYYYMMDD_description.sql`** (8-digit) with the example `20260225_secure_receipts_storage.sql`, but the baseline is 14-digit and the CLI requires 14. I named mine `20260803120000_receipt_notes.sql`, which pairs correctly — so the two migrations in this repo already disagree with each other, and the doc endorses the broken one.

Want me to fix that line in CLAUDE.md, and add the `migration repair --status applied` note for cleaning up the unpaired entry if you ever want the list to read straight?

Remote migration versions not found in local migrations directory.

Make sure your local git repo is up-to-date. If the error persists, try repairing the migration history table:
supabase migration repair --status reverted 20260803

And update local migrations to match remote database:

Initialising login role...
The remote database's migration history does not match local files in supabase/migrations directory.
Make sure your local git repo is up-to-date. If the error persists, try repairing the migration history table:
supabase migration repair --status reverted 20260803
supabase migration repair --status applied 20260803120000

**Do not run the second command the CLI suggested.** `supabase migration repair --status applied 20260803120000` would write a history row claiming my notes migration is already applied — when it isn't. The `notes` column would never get created, the CLI would never try again, and `dev:remote` would 400 on the Expenses page against a history table that says everything's fine. `repair` only edits the `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` bookkeeping table; it never runs or reverses SQL. The CLI is pattern-matching "local has it, remote doesn't → mark applied" with no idea whether it ran.

The first suggestion (`--status reverted 20260803`) is closer to right but incomplete on its own — it deletes the history row while the trigger stays live in the database, so remote would then claim the vendor-rules migration never ran.

I also need to correct my last message: I said don't rename that file. That was right *without* a repair; with one it's the actual fix, because repair lets you tell remote the truth about the new name.

**Confirm first** (dashboard SQL editor, 10 seconds) — that the thing the history row claims really is live:

```sql
select tgname from pg_trigger where tgname = 'apply_vendor_rule_after_insert';
```

If that returns a row, the vendor-rules migration genuinely is applied, and marking it applied under a new version is truthful bookkeeping rather than a lie.

**Then:**

```bash
# 1. local: give it a 14-digit version so the CLI can parse it
git mv supabase/migrations/20260803_apply_vendor_rules_on_receipt_insert.sql \
       supabase/migrations/20260803000000_apply_vendor_rules_on_receipt_insert.sql

# 2. remote: drop the unparseable row, record the real one
supabase migration repair --status reverted 20260803
supabase migration repair --status applied  20260803000000

# 3. verify before doing anything
supabase migration list        # should pair cleanly; only 20260803120000 pending
supabase db push --dry-run     # should list ONLY 20260803120000
supabase db push
```

Ordering stays correct after the rename: `20260726120000` < `20260803000000` < `20260803120000`.

Worth knowing: this is the same operation CLAUDE.md records from the baseline squash — "prod history was repaired to match (bookkeeping only)". Second time this repo has hit it, and the cause is the documented convention itself.

Two things I can do right now, both local and safe — say the word:
- the `git mv` in step 1,
- fix the CLAUDE.md line that says `YYYYMMDD_description.sql` (it should be `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`, matching the baseline and the CLI), plus a note about `migration repair` so the next person doesn't follow the CLI's suggestion blindly.

If the trigger query comes back **empty**, stop — that means remote history is claiming something that isn't there, which is a different and worse problem, and I'd want to look before you push anything.

**Naming convention:** `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql` — **14 digits, not 8** (e.g. `20260803120000_receipt_notes.sql`). The CLI parses the version as a full timestamp; an 8-digit name **breaks `supabase db push` and `db pull` outright** once it has been applied to remote. `20260803_apply_vendor_rules_on_receipt_insert.sql` was named that way (this line used to endorse it) and the result was `migration list` showing the same migration twice — unpaired, once per side, with the `Time (UTC)` column printing the raw string instead of a date — then `Remote migration versions not found in local migrations directory` on every push and pull. Fixed by renaming the file to `20260803000000_…` and repairing remote history; see below.

**`supabase migration repair` edits bookkeeping only — it never runs or reverses SQL.** So its own suggestions are not safe to follow blindly: when local has a migration remote lacks, the CLI proposes `--status applied <version>`, which would record your *unapplied* migration as done, and it then never runs. Before marking anything `applied`, confirm the schema object actually exists on remote (`select tgname from pg_trigger where …`, or check the column). Marking a version `reverted` deletes its history row without removing what it created, so pair it with a re-push of an idempotent migration or an `applied` repair under the corrected name. Prod history has now been repaired twice — once during the baseline squash, once for the 8-digit rename.

The CLI parses the version as a full timestamp; an 8-digit name **breaks `supabase db push` and `db pull` outright** once it has been applied to remote. `20260803_apply_vendor_rules_on_receipt_insert.sql` was named that way (this line used to endorse it) and the result was `migration list` showing the same migration twice — unpaired, once per side, with the `Time (UTC)` column printing the raw string instead of a date — then `Remote migration versions not found in local migrations directory` on every push and pull. Fixed by renaming the file to `20260803000000_…` and repairing remote history; see below.

**`supabase migration repair` edits bookkeeping only — it never runs or reverses SQL.** So its own suggestions are not safe to follow blindly: when local has a migration remote lacks, the CLI proposes `--status applied <version>`, which would record your *unapplied* migration as done, and it then never runs. Before marking anything `applied`, confirm the schema object actually exists on remote (`select tgname from pg_trigger where …`, or check the column). Marking a version `reverted` deletes its history row without removing what it created, so pair it with a re-push of an idempotent migration or an `applied` repair under the corrected name. Prod history has now been repaired twice — once during the baseline squash, once for the 8-digit rename.

1	# YFL Expense Tracker
2	
3	Family expense tracking app built with SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5, Supabase, and Tailwind CSS 4.
4	
5	## Commands
6	
7	```bash
8	npm run dev          # Dev server on localhost:5173
9	npm run build        # Production build
10	npm run verify       # The whole gate: check → check:deno → lint → server tests
11	npm run check        # Type checking (svelte-check, warnings are errors)
12	npm run check:deno   # Type-check supabase/functions/ (Deno — outside tsconfig scope)
13	npm run test:unit    # Vitest, single run (browser + node projects)
14	npm run test:watch   # Vitest in watch mode
15	npm run test:e2e     # Playwright e2e tests
16	npm test             # Full test suite (unit + e2e)
17	npm run lint         # Prettier check + ESLint (incl. Tailwind classes; warnings are errors)
18	npm run lint:fix     # ESLint autofix — most Tailwind class findings are fixable
19	npm run format       # Auto-format with Prettier
20	```
21	
22	## Architecture
23	
24	- **Routes:** `src/routes/` — SvelteKit file-based routing
25	- **Services:** `src/lib/services/` — Business logic (ExpenseService, ReceiptService, etc.). Some use DI (take Supabase client as param), others use singleton pattern with module-level import.
26	- **Models:** `src/lib/models/` — TypeScript data models
27	- **Components:** `src/lib/components/` — Reusable Svelte components
28	- **Utils:** `src/lib/utils/` — Helper functions with co-located `.spec.ts` tests
29	- **Server:** `src/lib/server/` — Server-only code (file validation, OCR processing)
30	- **CSV Parsers:** `src/lib/services/csvParsers/` — Bank-specific CSV parsers (Amex, PC Financial, RBC, TD, Simplii, EQ Bank, Wealth Simple) with `BaseCSVParser` and `CSVParserFactory` for auto-detection
31	- **Docs:** `docs/` — Project documentation. `docs/adr/` (architecture decision records), `docs/plans/` (design docs — **when the work is done, `git mv` the plan to `docs/plans-done/`**, same reason and same depth as `prd-done/`, so its `../` links keep working; fix inbound links), `docs/prd-*.md` (active PRDs — in-file `**Status:**` front-matter carries the detail; **when a PRD is finished, `git mv` it to `docs/prd-done/`** so done-vs-active is visible from `ls` without opening files, and fix its now-one-level-deeper relative links plus any inbound links), `docs/product-backlog.md` (the single working list — features, bugs, engineering, and open refactoring items as one-liners) plus `docs/refactoring-backlog.md` (detailed RF-NN reference, not a separate to-do list), `docs/domain-model.md` (ubiquitous-language glossary). Prefer `docs/` over root for any new note or plan; the root keeps only `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
32	- **Migrations:** `supabase/migrations/` — SQL migrations (schema + RLS policies)
33	
34	## Supabase Migrations
35	
36	Migrations live in `supabase/migrations/` as numbered SQL files. The project is linked to the remote Supabase project (`YFL Expense Tracker`, region `ca-central-1`).
37	
38	```bash
39	supabase migration list           # Show local vs remote migration status
40	supabase db push                  # Push pending migrations to remote database
41	supabase db push --dry-run        # Preview what would be applied without running
42	supabase migration new <name>     # Create a new empty migration file
43	supabase db diff --schema public  # Generate migration from local schema changes
44	supabase db reset                 # Reset local DB and re-run all migrations (destructive)
45	```
46	
47	**Naming convention:** `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql` — **14 digits, not 8** (e.g. `20260803120000_receipt_notes.sql`). The CLI parses the version as a full timestamp; an 8-digit name **breaks `supabase db push` and `db pull` outright** once it has been applied to remote. `20260803_apply_vendor_rules_on_receipt_insert.sql` was named that way (this line used to endorse it) and the result was `migration list` showing the same migration twice — unpaired, once per side, with the `Time (UTC)` column printing the raw string instead of a date — then `Remote migration versions not found in local migrations directory` on every push and pull. Fixed by renaming the file to `20260803000000_…` and repairing remote history; see below.
48	
49	**`supabase migration repair` edits bookkeeping only — it never runs or reverses SQL.** So its own suggestions are not safe to follow blindly: when local has a migration remote lacks, the CLI proposes `--status applied <version>`, which would record your _unapplied_ migration as done, and it then never runs. Before marking anything `applied`, confirm the schema object actually exists on remote (`select tgname from pg_trigger where …`, or check the column). Marking a version `reverted` deletes its history row without removing what it created, so pair it with a re-push of an idempotent migration or an `applied` repair under the corrected name. Prod history has now been repaired twice — once during the baseline squash, once for the 8-digit rename.
50	
51	**Squashed to a baseline (2026-07-26).** `supabase/migrations/` holds one file,
52	`20260726120000_baseline.sql`; the 31 predecessors are in `supabase/migrations-archive/`. They
53	could not rebuild the DB from scratch — replay died at `007` with `relation "public.families" does
54	not exist` because `families` was created by hand in the dashboard and only captured later by the
55	`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump, which sorts _after_ `007`. Prod history was repaired to
56	match (bookkeeping only). **The baseline's storage section is hand-maintained** — `supabase db
57	dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are appended
58	manually at the end of the file. Any storage change must be reflected there too. Verify every new
59	migration with `npm run db:reset` before pushing. See `docs/local-dev.md`.
60	
61	**Important:** The migration role does NOT own `storage.objects`, so `COMMENT ON POLICY` and `ALTER TABLE` on storage tables will fail. Stick to `CREATE POLICY` / `DROP POLICY` / `UPDATE storage.buckets` for storage changes.
62	
63	## Key Patterns
64	
65	- **Expenses are computed, not stored.** No "expenses" table — expenses are joins of receipts + expense_categories + categories. Each receipt maps to exactly one expense (1:1).
66	- **All data is family-scoped.** Users belong to families via `family_members`. RLS policies enforce family-level access on receipts, transactions, categories, and vendor rules.
67	- **Receipt storage is private.** The `receipts` bucket is private — all file access uses signed URLs via `getSignedReceiptUrl()` from `src/lib/utils/signedUrl.ts`. Pages cache signed URLs in a reactive `signedUrls` map loaded via `$effect`. OCR uses short-lived signed URLs (5 min expiry). Display uses 1-hour expiry.
68	- **Storage RLS is family-scoped for reads.** Family members can read each other's receipt files. Write/delete is restricted to the file owner (path prefix = `user_id`).
69	- **Adding a column to `receipts` means editing three hand-maintained lists, and the compiler checks none of them.** They are `ReceiptService.#EDITABLE_FIELDS` (an allow-list — a field missing from it is silently stripped from every `update()`, no error, the value just never saves), `buildReceiptPatch` in `src/lib/utils/receiptPatch.ts` (what the edit modal actually sends, shared by the Receipts, Reconciliation and Expenses pages), and the `isDirty` comparison in `ReceiptEditModal.svelte` (miss it and closing the modal discards an unsaved edit **with no prompt**). It used to be five — the three pages each hand-wrote their own patch literal and had already drifted from one another. Do not reintroduce a per-page patch object. Two related rules: **`buildReceiptPatch` carries only what the modal can edit**, because writing back a field the modal merely read turns any save into a lost update; and **`suspicious_date` belongs to `ReceiptService.update` alone**, which forces it to `false` whenever `transaction_date` is present — a page-level copy of that rule is dead code, which is exactly what the old Receipts literal was, under a comment claiming the opposite.

**What I changed:**
- `20260803_apply_vendor_rules_on_receipt_insert.sql` → `20260803000000_…` (14-digit)
- The code comment in `ReceiptService.ts:283` that pointed at the old filename
- CLAUDE.md: the naming convention now says **14 digits, not 8**, explains the exact symptom this produced, and adds a paragraph on `migration repair` — specifically that its own suggestions aren't safe to follow blindly, since it edits bookkeeping without running SQL

**Your turn — the two remote commands.** These touch production history, so they're yours to run:

```bash
supabase migration repair --status reverted 20260803
supabase migration repair --status applied  20260803000000
```

The second is now truthful: `apply_vendor_rule_after_insert` exists on remote, so recording it as applied under the corrected name matches reality.

Then confirm before pushing:

```bash
supabase migration list      # three rows, all paired; 20260803120000 pending
supabase db push --dry-run   # should name ONLY 20260803120000
supabase db push
```

If `--dry-run` lists anything other than `20260803120000` alone, stop and show me.

After that, `npm run dev:remote` will have the `notes` column and the feature works end to end. Two reminders from earlier that still stand: that dev server writes to **real family data**, and `buildReceiptPatch` changed what every receipt save sends — not just notes — so the first Save you do against prod is exercising new code on real records.

Still not committed, per CLAUDE.md. Everything's staged, including the rename.

- `20260726120000` — baseline, paired ✓
- `20260803000000` — vendor rules, **paired** ✓ (was the duplicated, unpaired pair)
- `20260803120000` — notes, local only, genuinely pending ✓

One migration to apply, which is the correct state. Go ahead:

```bash
supabase db push --dry-run   # expect only 20260803120000
supabase db push
```

Then `npm run dev:remote` will have the column.

After it lands, worth a quick sanity check in the dashboard that the constraint came across too, not just the column:

```sql
select conname from pg_constraint where conname = 'receipts_notes_length';
```

That's the half a plain column-existence check would miss, and it's the thing actually enforcing 1024.

Then the feature is exercisable: open a receipt, type a note, save, and it should appear truncated under the merchant name on both the Receipts and Expenses lists. The two cautions stand — real family data, and every Save now goes through `buildReceiptPatch`, so you're exercising the changed save path on real receipts, not just the note field.
